paragraphs: D-Fend Solutions sells counter-drone systems to military, law enforcement and homeland security agencies. Its core product, EnforceAir, detects a rogue drone, takes control of it through a radio-frequency cyber takeover and brings it to a safe landing. The company describes the approach as non-kinetic and AI-enhanced, built for sensitive and challenging environments.

EnforceAir can operate autonomously or under manual control, and it detects, locates and identifies rogue drones in a protected airspace before taking them over. It is sold in several deployment packages, including a Homeland Security & Law Enforcement Bundle and two tactical configurations, EnforceAir PLUS and EnforceAir2. EnforceAir PLUS, launched in August 2025, adds radar and a jammer to the RF-cyber layer. Beyond agencies, the company says the system has been chosen for large-scale events at stadiums, arenas and open-air venues and for VIP protection.

In an August 2026 press release the company says EnforceAir provided counter-drone security across World Cup host cities and was adopted by more than 20 public safety agencies. Chairman and CEO Zohar Halachmi co-founded the company after founding two mobile and enterprise application start-ups. Its U.S. arm, D-Fend Solutions AD, Inc., is located in McLean, Virginia. In June 2026 the company announced an agreement to be acquired by Motorola Solutions. Its newsroom now states that it has officially joined Motorola Solutions.

quote.text: To truly take full control of a dangerous drone situation, the key is taking control of the drone itself, and staying in control throughout the incident.

RF cyber-driven, non-kinetic, AI-enhanced, counter-drone takeover technology for sensitive and challenging environments.

paragraphs: Transoft Solutions makes software for the people who plan, design and operate transportation systems. Its work spans aviation, civil infrastructure, transportation and operational professionals. On the aviation side that means specialized software to plan, analyze and optimize airport and airspace operations.

The company started in 1991, when co-founder Milton Carrasco developed a vehicle tracking program called AutoTURN. That product grew out of his master's thesis on computerized vehicle-turning simulation. The range has widened since through in-house development and strategic acquisitions. One executive is credited with merging AeroTURN and PathPlanner into AviPLAN.

The company reports more than 100,000 customers in over 150 countries. Clients are described as government agencies at the federal, state, county and municipal levels, along with major international airports and engineering and architectural design firms. Headquarters are in British Columbia, Canada, with further offices in the United States, Australia, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Belgium, Germany, France, Sweden, Spain, India and China.

paragraphs: Kova Corp sells communication, recording and alerting software for public safety organizations and for enterprises. The products page splits the catalogue into public safety solutions, enterprise workforce optimization solutions and an emergency alerting solution.

KEANS, the KOVA Emergency Alert Notification System, links multiple locations, agencies, business partners and public address systems such as loudspeakers, bull horns and audio distribution repeaters. KAMS, the Kova Alarm Monitoring Solution, handles hardware monitoring, captures SNMP alerts and OS events, and can monitor data streams such as CDR, P25 traffic and RTP.

The workforce optimization page offers contact centers a platform for multimedia recording, evaluation and archiving of calls, plus an Enterprise Feedback Management survey platform and a Workforce Management solution. The about page names 911 call centers and emergency responders as the people those public safety solutions serve. The about page also cites a recorder installed for the Port Authority of NY/NJ after the loss of its Emergency Operations Center.

quote.text: Whether your organization is searching for enterprise workforce optimization solutions, public safety solutions, or a emergency alerting solution, KOVA has the products and the know-how to customize a solution to fit your unique needs.

provenance.quote: Kova Corp delivers reliable solutions for enterprise and security intelligence and alerting, efforts supported by our partnerships with global leaders in public safety.

Whether your organization is searching for enterprise workforce optimization solutions, public safety solutions, or a emergency alerting solution, KOVA has the products and the know-how to customize a solution to fit your unique needs.

KEANS (KOVA Emergency Alert Notification System) provides reliable, simultaneous communication between multiple locations, agencies, business partners, and public address systems (such as loudspeakers, bull horns, and audio distribution repeaters).

KAMS provides not only the typical Hardware monitoring (CPU usage, memory, drive space, temperature, etc.) along with capturing SNMP alerts and OS events, but also can monitor critical data streams like CDR, P25 traffic, and RTP.
Kova recording solutions for contact centers provide a high performance platform for the multimedia recording, evaluation, and archiving of calls.

Our public safety solutions enable 911 call centers to function more efficiently, allow emergency responders to instantly share vital information, and make it possible to record and decipher data gathered.
KOVA offered immediate assistance to the Port Authority of NY/NJ, when it lost its Emergency Operations Center on 9/11. Within twenty-four hours, KOVA installed a new recorder at a temporary site.

paragraphs: Reunitus sells lost and found management and baggage resolution through software and managed service offerings. The offering is grouped into baggage resolution, lost item resolution, and unclaimed item monetization. paragraphs: Frequentis supplies communication and information systems for control centres with safety-critical tasks. The work splits between air traffic management, civil and military, and public safety and transport.

On the public safety side the buyers are police, fire brigades, ambulance services, coastguards and port authorities. Voice communication for air traffic control is the anchor, and the company puts its share of that market at around 30%. It also sells aeronautical information management and aeronautical message handling systems. Current development centres on digital remote tower technology, drone management and 5G/LTE in safety-critical applications.

The Austrian company is headquartered in Vienna and was founded in 1947. It keeps a network of branches, subsidiaries and local representatives in more than 50 countries. Around 550 customers in approximately 150 countries rely on its know-how, by its own count. Installed operator positions number around 49,000 worldwide. More than 75% of employees come from science, technology, engineering and mathematics backgrounds.

paragraphs: Gatekeeper Systems sells video recording and data systems for transportation, meant to make travel safer for children, passengers, and public safety personnel across several modes. The company says it uses AI, video analytics, thermal cameras, and mobile data collectors to inter-connect public transit assets within intelligent transportation systems.

Its mobile data collectors gather video and audio along with GPS tracking and door open and close events, analyzing the data on the bus itself. Those units are ruggedized and crashworthy, serving as black boxes that hold data for accident investigations. Recorders take analog and IP channels at up to 1080P and 30 frames per second, with independently selectable resolutions. Drive caddies have passed MIL SPEC 810F for shock and vibration, and a thermal system warms the hard drive to its prescribed operating temperature before writing or reading in cold weather.

Fleet software called G4 Vision centralizes system health checks, driver behavior analysis, video management, live streaming, GPS, routing and mapping, and student tracking. An Automated Lane Enforcement product for transit buses is named on the home page. The company describes a Platform-as-a-Service business model. Testimonials on that page are attributed to school district transportation directors.

before.description: Cloud identity management system (IDMS) purpose-built for US airport badge offices: applications, renewals, TSA audit compliance, training and scheduling, integrated with fingerprint, PACS (LenelS2) and training platforms.

paragraphs: AirBadge sells identity management software to airports in the United States, aimed at the badge office that issues and renews credentials. The company says it puts all of its resources into aviation so the software fits airport operations and TSA regulations. The product is described as built for 1542 and part 139 airports.

Applicants and badge holders enter their own details into the system. Those details are then sent directly to integrated systems, which removes a round of rekeying. It automates badge applications, appointment scheduling, training and testing, and cuts manual entry at fingerprinting, physical access control and TSC. paragraphs: RideCo sells on-demand transit software that agencies use to plan, operate, and optimize service productivity while reducing transit costs. The software covers paratransit and microtransit, and the company attributes it to patented technology.

Products listed on the site include the Passenger App, the Driver App, Operations Center, Data Insights, Profile Manager, and Flex Fleets. The Passenger App lets riders request on-demand trips, preschedule them, or book recurring rides, and it is available on smartphones and on a standard web browser. Operations Center is a dashboard suite for streamlining operations and service monitoring in a transit dispatch center, with standardized and custom reports inside it.

Customers named on the site include MTA New York City Transit, which awarded a contract for its Access-A-Ride paratransit service. Other agencies named include the Regional Transportation Commission of Southern Nevada and Metropolitan Atlanta Rapid Transit Authority, both for paratransit service.

quote.text: Together with RideCo, transit agencies can transform mobility for today and tomorrow.

provenance.quote: Our software is designed to help you plan, operate, and optimize service productivity while reducing your transit costs.
With patented technology, RideCo’s on-demand paratransit and microtransit software is changing the way agencies deliver mobility to their communities.
In-vehicle driver facing application for automated vehicle location, mobile data communication, and real-time dispatch and data collection.
Using the Passenger App, riders can request on-demand trips or preschedule them in advance, book recurring rides, or schedule multiple trips at a time.
Reporting within Operations Center provides user-driven access to both standardized and custom reports.

paragraphs: Gatekeeper Systems sells video recording and data systems for transportation, meant to make travel safer for children, passengers, and public safety personnel across several modes. The company says it uses AI, video analytics, thermal cameras, and mobile data collectors to inter-connect public transit assets within intelligent transportation systems.

Its mobile data collectors gather video and audio along with GPS tracking and door open and close events, analyzing the data on the bus itself. Those units are ruggedized and crashworthy, serving as black boxes that hold data for accident investigations. Recorders take analog and IP channels at up to 1080P and 30 frames per second, with independently selectable resolutions. Drive caddies have passed MIL SPEC 810F for shock and vibration, and a thermal system warms the hard drive to its prescribed operating temperature before writing or reading in cold weather.

Fleet software called G4 Vision centralizes system health checks, driver behavior analysis, video management, live streaming, GPS, routing and mapping, and student tracking. An Automated Lane Enforcement product for transit buses is named on the home page. The company describes a Platform-as-a-Service business model. Testimonials on that page are attributed to school district transportation directors.

paragraphs: GIRO makes software for the organizations that run public transport and postal delivery services, covering the work from planning through daily operations. Its two product families, HASTUS and GeoRoute, are in use in more than 30 countries.

The company grounds the work in knowledge of the problems those operators face day to day. GIRO states that more than 30% of its resources go to research and development. New ideas and solutions are developed with clients and validated by groups of users around the world.

GIRO was founded in the 1970s through the work of a Université de Montréal student and his professor. That early work paved the way for the creation of both products. The company counts over 40 years of experience in the field. It also notes a ranking among the 300 largest companies in Quebec.

paragraphs: March Networks sells video surveillance systems for multi-site organizations, built from IP cameras, recorders, encoders and other hardware sold as one portfolio. Command Enterprise Software is the management layer for deploying and maintaining those video surveillance resources across a customer site. Searchlight, sold on premise or as a cloud service, turns the recorded video into loss prevention and business intelligence reporting.

The analytics catalogue covers people counting, heatmaps, dwell time, license plate recognition, and alerts for loitering, intrusion and blocked emergency exits. Detection runs on the AI Series cameras and on X-Series recorders built with NVIDIA system-on-chip technology, with alerts sent as mobile push notifications.

The company dates its founding to 2000 and puts retail, banking and transportation at the front of the industries it serves. The homepage counts more than 1,730 financial institutions, over 675 retailers and more than 735 commercial and industrial customers in over 75 countries. March Networks and VIVOTEK have merged their branded video security businesses, and the merged portfolio is presented across cloud, hybrid and on premise environments.

paragraphs: Interloc Solutions sells consulting and software for IBM Maximo, and the company describes a complete focus on Maximo across its services. Interloc also sells Mobile Informer, its own native app platform for Maximo mobility. A hosting service the pages call Maximo in the Cloud is offered alongside it. The consulting covers Maximo industry solutions and add-ons, among them Maximo Spatial Asset Management, Maximo Linear Asset Management, and the Maximo ERP Adapter.

Mobile Informer Work Management, shortened to iWM, runs on native applications and gives maintenance workers work orders, labor hours, meter readings and failure records on a device, online or offline. Mobile Informer Inventory Management, shortened to iIM, covers storeroom tasks such as issue, return, transfer, receipt and cycle count, and works with barcode readers and printers.

Testimonials on the home page are credited to Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART), to AUA Airport, and to Morgan Foods. The New York City Housing Authority is quoted on the work management page about staff recording data on mobile devices.

quote.text: Give your mobile workforce what they need, while enhancing operational effectiveness and maximizing your return on your asset management investment.

provenance.quote: With hundreds of years of combined experience and 100% focus on Maximo, Interloc provides all the support and expertise you’ll need to get the most out of your Maximo software systems.
Interloc’s user-friendly, native app platform provides enhanced mobility capabilities to help you cut costs and boost ROI.
Access all the major hosting providers with Interloc’s Maximo Cloud hosting service.
Interloc is well versed in Maximo’s industry solutions and add-ons
iWM features native applications that provide fast, responsive performance while making full use of device capabilities
Perform storeroom activities from a single app, including: issue/return items receive purchase orders, transfer items between store-rooms, and perform cycle counts.
Interloc’s Mobile Informer over Maximo solution has been the reliable, affordable and flexible solution to do just that at AUA Airport.
Much like a delivery driver can record detailed transactional data via a mobile device, NYCHA maintenance and skilled trades staff are now able to do the same.

before.description: Mobile video surveillance, DVRs, and MotoTrax analytics for transit, school, and municipal fleets - exhibited at CTAA EXPO 2026, NAPT Summit 2026

paragraphs: AngelTrax sells mobile video surveillance systems built for transportation safety. The company describes its customers as student transportation, mass transit, fleet, locomotive, and waste operations.

On a school bus, interior, exterior, stop-arm, and windshield views cover students, drivers, and transportation staff. Footage leaves the vehicle two ways, and a cellular link carries live view, active tracking, and instant notifications. Wi-Fi handles automated downloads once vehicles return to range. Video and data can be hosted by AngelTrax at its secure U.S. data center rather than handed to a third party. Its online software covers live view, downloads, vehicle location, health reporting, stop-arm workflows, and driver behavior. Driver behavior events arrive with video meant to support coaching, claims response, and accountability.

The company page dates the business to 2006. It reports 250,000 active systems operating worldwide. It also states $2.5M spent on research and development yearly. The same page describes a SOC 2 Type II-compliant data center for data security.

paragraphs: SilverRide runs an assisted transportation platform for older adults and people with disabilities, licensed as a Transportation Network Company in 18 states. The driver network is made up of credentialed independent contractors using their own vehicles across 35+ major metro areas.

The company works three ways: paratransit partnerships with transit agencies, contract services for PACE and healthcare organizations, and direct booking for riders and their families. For transit agencies the service is ADA-compliant paratransit at scale, including complementary service, overflow capacity, premium tiers, and same-day trips. For PACE programs and healthcare organizations the service is door-through-door, with the driver escorting riders from inside the pickup location into the destination.
SilverRide was founded in 2006 by Jeff Maltz and Susan Steiner Saal. The company reports more than one million rides every year with 95% on-time performance.

before.name: CITYROVER
before.description: AI dashcams (EDGE/PULSE) for automated pothole and road-defect detection for public works - exhibited at CTAA EXPO 2026

paragraphs: CITYROVER sells smart cameras and software that governments mount in vehicles already driving their streets, so road problems get spotted without a dedicated inspection trip. The stated aim is taking over inspection work that agencies would otherwise do by hand.

Detection happens on the camera itself, which uploads what it finds to the cloud for review. Staff get notifications carrying the location and images of the issue. The camera picks out potholes, manholes, dumped garbage, transit infrastructure problems and signs. Two other families sit beside it: PULSE for pavement rating, pavement markings and survey imagery, and COMPANION, an app for inspectors and work crews.

Government inspectors are the main users, reporting maintenance and operations issues automatically. An open API and off-the-shelf connectors move the data into systems an agency already runs. The site claims hundreds of governments as customers.

before.name: Consat
before.description: Consat Telematics real-time CAD/AVL, passenger info, and electromobility analytics (NA office Sudbury ON)

paragraphs: Consat Telematics is a Swedish provider of public transportation systems, founded in 1986 and operating across Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Australia, Canada, and Brazil. The wider Consat group reports offices on five continents and more than 250 employees.

The transit offering is modular, covering electromobility for electric fleet monitoring and smart charging as well as traffic control and monitoring for real-time fleet oversight and incident management. Passenger information delivers accurate, real-time updates to riders both onboard and offboard. Every part is described as multivendor and multimodal compatible, deployable in cloud, on-premise, or data centre environments. Support runs end to end, from installation and integration through maintenance and training.

The hardware and software are installed on more than 40,000 vehicles globally. Named customers include Skyss in Norway, Tide Buss in Sweden, Ventura Bus Lines in Australia, and Din Tur in Sweden. A headline on the same page announces Bonnier Capital becoming a strategic partner in Consat Telematics. The company states that it is certified as a Great Place to Work for 2024 and 2025.

paragraphs: Ontra Mobility sells a planning platform that transit agencies use to model travel demand and generate optimized routes and on-demand zones before committing to service changes. The platform encodes budget, fleet, service standards, and agency feedback as constraints, and builds phased rollout plans for pilots and long-term planning. Analysis tools in the platform map origin-destination trip flows, load factors by route and time period, isochrone coverage, and census data.

A second product is a white-labeled trip planner app that carries the operator's branding and ingests GTFS and GTFS-RT feeds for schedules, vehicle positions, and service alerts. Ontra also sells operations software for bus, shuttle, and paratransit services, with a monitor app for fleet visibility, a driver app, and a rider app for on-demand trips. The operations stack also includes rider and driver applications for iOS and Android plus dashboard, analysis, and admin tools.

The white-label app is aimed at transit agencies, universities and campuses, hospitals and medical centers, corporate campuses, events and conferences, and apartment complexes. Ontra Mobility partners with the City of Fresno on a Transit On-Demand Feasibility Study. Ontra was selected for Transit Tech Lab to conduct a proof of concept with agency partners including MTA NYCT and LIRR.

paragraphs: O-CITY is an automated fare collection platform for public transport operators and municipalities, and the payment technology behind it comes from BPC. The platform digitalises the payment process end-to-end, and travellers use a mobile or a payment card rather than paper tickets. Citizens and tourists can pay with smart cards, contactless Visa, MasterCard or UnionPay, mobile wallets, and QR codes.

These pages say the platform is sold to transport agencies, governments and merchants for self-service digital ticketing across their cities. For operators, account-based ticketing is described as reduced costs, improved efficiency and easier fare management. Fares can be based on route, type of transport or service, or traveller status such as student or senior.

Deployment options include on-premise, PaaS, SaaS or fully managed operations, on existing transport or merchant terminals. A case study on the platform page describes Bishkek moving away from the use of cash. Another case study describes a Ministry of Transport automating public transport fare collection.

before.description: Solar smart bus stops with edge AI plus the ORA platform: signage, lane enforcement, passenger counting

paragraphs: BusPas upgrades, connects and modernizes urban furniture, starting with bus stops. It equips that furniture with sensors and edge computing meant to improve transit, protect user privacy and enhance security. The buyers are municipalities and transit agencies looking to optimize operations and improve services.

The ORA Ecosystem is the platform side, giving public transit agencies, cities and their officials access to data services linked to infrastructure within their municipality. The stops display real-time bus wait times and occupancy, count waiting passengers, and track boarding and alighting to analyze connections and origins and destinations. The system can also send specific requests to control traffic lights for buses and emergency vehicles. SaferSmart Zones is a turnkey bus and transit lane enforcement offering. Solar panels are added to minimize dependence on the grid. The products are described as a modular ecosystem of solar-powered, AI-enabled street infrastructure for transit reliability, safety, enforcement and passenger experience.

The company says it started in 2017. It works through standing contracts, so new legislation or an RFP is not required. A statement on the site is attributed to the mayor of Sainte-Julie, Québec. A headline says its smart stop technology was deployed across the TTC network ahead of the FIFA World Cup 2026.

paragraphs: Aesys builds passenger information displays for intercity, regional and metropolitan rail. It also makes variable message signs carrying traffic and safety information on highways, in tunnels and in cities. At airports its flight information displays run from the runway to the baggage area. A further line covers industrial displays made to hold up in harsh environments.

Displays carrying road information are built to comply with a European standard for variable message signs. Design and production are handled internally at the Bergamo headquarters. Testing starts early, from the first stages of prototyping. Software staff have written interfaces for standard protocols such as NTCIP, DisplayML, Modbus and TLS.

The company says it has been growing since 1977. It reports over 400 employees dedicated to product excellence. Sales offices sit in Germany, Spain and the United States. Certifications listed include a quality management system under ISO 9001.

paragraphs: Samsara sells a platform to organizations that run vehicles and equipment, pitched on improving safety, lowering costs and changing how operations work. For fleets it covers live GPS tracking, vehicle diagnostics, fuel analytics and compliance reporting. The company presents this as one platform working across every part of an operation rather than separate tools.

Its cameras pair safety detections with video that managers can pull on demand. The company says the system watches for drowsiness, distraction, tailgating and forward collision risk. It states that these are caught in real time and trigger an in-cab alert before a manager is involved. A multicamera option adds up to four auxiliary HD feeds for visibility around the vehicle. A separate site product brings third-party cameras at facilities into a cloud dashboard for onboarding and troubleshooting.

The camera pages list transportation and logistics, field services, construction, public sector and essential services among the industries served. For school districts the company describes arm-mounted cameras that enforce school bus stop-arm compliance during pickups and drop-offs. Among its customer stories is one saying the City of El Paso recovered $1.3M in assets and reduced accidents by 29%. A site camera gateway is listed as compliant with the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019.

paragraphs: Piper Networks is a rail engineering solutions provider and systems integrator working in transportation technologies. before.name: Spare

paragraphs: Spare sells operations software that a public transit agency runs its service on. The modes it covers include paratransit, microtransit and fixed route, along with asset management.

In one system an agency handles scheduling and dispatch, the rider experience, fleet health, and compliance and reporting. Because paratransit trips are often contracted out, the platform pulls trips from different providers into one place. Eligibility applications and rider records are digitized, which the company says speeds up the review process. On the fixed route side, an agency can plan service, publish a GTFS feed, build schedules and run live operations together. A voice assistant answers rider calls for bookings, arrival times and common questions.

The platform is described as built to meet ADA, NTD and grant reporting requirements. It connects through open APIs, GTFS, AVL feeds and single sign-on rather than replacing what a technology team already runs. Spare puts its reach at more than 230 communities. Its fixed route page describes coordinating a large event shuttle for LA Metro.

paragraphs: LYT sells signal priority software that gives buses and emergency vehicles a green light at intersections, and it runs on the signal controllers and vehicle equipment an agency already has. The platform is described as cloud-based software billed as an operating expense, with predictable annual costs rather than a capital purchase.

For transit agencies, the platform models traffic and adjusts signal timing so that buses keep to schedule. For fire departments and for EMS and police, it preempts the signals ahead of responding vehicles as they approach an intersection.

LYT states that it maintains SOC 2 Type 2 compliance and that the platform is purpose-built for public agencies. Procurement routes listed on the page include a cooperative contract in Washington, a rider contract with LA Metro, and NEORide for member agencies.

before.name: TransTrack Solutions Group
before.description: Transit performance data warehousing, BI, and automated NTD reporting (Modaxo brand) - exhibited at CTAA EXPO 2026

paragraphs: TransTrack Systems writes software for public transit agencies that pulls scattered operating data into one place so performance can be watched and reported. The main application collects data from across an agency so teams can follow trends and produce the reports decisions rest on.

Much of the appeal is federal reporting: agency data is applied automatically to the required National Transit Database forms, which the company says turns most of the annual filing from weeks of work into days. A companion analytics product presents the same operating data as dashboards, reports and metrics an agency can adjust. The point of it, in the company's framing, is to replace manual spreadsheets and disconnected systems and keep the numbers behind federal funding accurate.

The firm was formed in 2002 by transit management professionals. More than twenty years on, it describes its business as helping agencies turn operating data into better decisions. Alongside the software it lists consulting work such as transit financial planning and cost analyses. The platform itself was built with transit professionals involved.

paragraphs: Esri builds ArcGIS, its geographic information system software for mapping and spatial analysis. The company describes itself as the global market leader in GIS software, location intelligence, and mapping. Its stated audience is business, government, and society.

ArcGIS is presented as enterprise technology that integrates and connects data through the context of geography. The premise is that hidden patterns, trends, and relationships emerge once data is visualized and analyzed on a map. Beyond maps and analysis, the company says its technology speeds data sharing and collaboration. For agencies that want to keep everything in house, there is a self-hosted edition for mapping, analytics, and data management.

Esri says it has supported customers with geographic science and geospatial analytics since 1969. Officials working in public safety, transportation, infrastructure, health and human services, and other fields use the technology to support high-level decisions. At the local level, the company says community leaders apply it to economic development, public works, and urban planning. Published stories include the US Census Bureau modernizing its entire census process with GIS.

before.name: Connixt
before.description: iMarq mobile asset maintenance and MRO platform for transit, rail, and fleets

paragraphs: Connixt sells iMarq, a mobile-first application built for field crews, technicians and mechanics to digitize and automate data collection, paperwork, processes and workflows. The company aims it at fleets, rail, transit, manufacturing, heavy engineering and facilities.

There are native apps for iOS and Android. They run on phones and tablets, both online and offline. Crews record asset details in the organization's own forms, on their own devices, in real time. An assistant called iBot puts institutional knowledge, troubleshooting guidance and compliance support in front of frontline teams, while reporting lets users reach their data on any device and track asset status.

Public agency case studies include a transportation department whose traffic signal division used the customizable mobile app to digitize work orders and improve transparency. Another covers Metrolink, which automated the train delay reporting its conductors had been doing on paper. The company reports winning two Progressive Railroading Reader's Choice Awards for a second consecutive year. It is run by two co-founders, Satish and Prabhu, described as industry veterans, and the site cites a 4.8 rating on Capterra.

before.name: Axon Vibe
before.description: Mobility behavior platform powering operator apps: journey detection, BIBO ticketing (built the MTA app)

paragraphs: Axon Vibe sells a smartphone-based, multi-modal mobility platform to public transport operators and authorities. The idea is to match a rider's predicted travel patterns against real-time traffic on roads and rail, then offer more efficient and less polluting travel options.

Patented location tracking predicts what people are going to do next, and psychological communication interventions are used to shift their behaviour. Riders who respond are rewarded with travel fare incentives financed by green governmental funds, plus rewards provided by local merchants. The platform is also sold to enable automatic ticketing, incentivise behaviour change and optimise customer flow management. For cities, understanding why and how people travel in real time is presented as the basis for more accurate planning.

Door-to-door journey detection powers Deutsche Bahn check-in and be-out ticketing, for example in Greater Nuremberg. The Metropolitan Transportation Authority launched its official MTA app in March 2024. Founded in 2014, the company describes a team of more than 100 software engineers, data scientists, location analytics experts, psychologists and communication specialists. Its predecessor Endoxon delivered core technology for Google Maps and was acquired by Google in 2006.

paragraphs: Knaq sells hardware sensors and cloud software that monitor industrial equipment which is not otherwise connected. The sensors are made in house, installed without invasive work, and send data over cellular connections. They capture vibration, temperature, runtime, and operational behavior, and the stated install time is 30 to 120 minutes on legacy and modern equipment. A cloud dashboard shows live status and asset health across a portfolio, and machine learning models identify early signs of degradation before failures occur.

Knaq describes the equipment it monitors as critical infrastructure across airports, transit systems, hospitals, universities, and industrial facilities. For transit agencies the stated value is early identification of failures that lead to station outages and accessibility violations. Large real estate portfolios are listed as another buyer group, with tenant disruption and contractor performance named as concerns.

The about page names Sound Transit as a client that paired the platform with its own maintenance operation to reduce elevator and escalator unreported time. The platform connects to CMMS platforms and BMS through the Knaq API, so equipment data reaches systems facilities teams already run.

before.name: Miovision
before.description: Traffic data collection and smart intersection technology - exhibited at IAFC FRI 2026

paragraphs: Miovision sells traffic data collection tools meant to give planners the accurate, verifiable data their mobility plans depend on. It also sells detection equipment that improves signal performance by responding to real-world road user demand, from bicycles to articulated trucks. Its Opticom line clears the path for emergency fleets without re-timing entire corridors.

Portable devices capture comprehensive multimodal count data including cars, trucks, pedestrians and bikes. A newer optimization product replaces manual five-year retiming cycles with iterative, objective-based optimization that the company says cuts manual effort by up to half. Engineers compare plans side-by-side, validate against industry standards, and push updates directly to field controllers without manual data re-entry.

The company says that since 2005 it has had 2,000 customers in 68 countries and 13,000 cities, with 30 billion vehicles and 1.5 billion pedestrians counted. It lists more than 300 detection customers in North America. Detroit partnered with Miovision to upgrade over 600 intersections. In San Rafael, police and fire vehicles now receive signal priority at 53 intersections.

before.name: Avail Technologies
before.description: myAvail enterprise transit management ITS and CAD/AVL for mid-size US agencies

paragraphs: Avail Technologies sells enterprise transit management software to public transit agencies. The company states that its target market is transit operators with medium-sized fleets.

The myAvail platform covers vehicle location, dispatching, workforce management, reporting, and rider communications, so a team works from one connected system rather than several tools. A single shared database moves data throughout the organization. Dispatchers see where every bus and driver is, and incidents are tracked as they occur. Business intelligence dashboards report metrics in real time, which the company frames as a way to improve efficiency, justify funding requests, and demonstrate compliance. Features can be added to the platform as an agency's needs grow, and the company says myAvail ships multiple platform updates a year.

Founded in 1999, Avail describes a family-oriented staff working hand-in-hand with transit professionals. It says it has stayed a mid-sized company by design. An announcement on the site names Rick Spangler as president and chief executive as the company continues a transition to full employee ownership.

before.name: Hayden AI
before.description: Bus-mounted AI cameras enforcing bus lanes and stops for transit agencies

paragraphs: Hayden AI mounts cameras on transit buses so cities can catch vehicles that block bus lanes and stops. The system pairs vision AI with hardware built for the vehicle and reads the street around it as the bus drives.

Automated bus lane enforcement is the flagship product, meant to clear unauthorized parking and raise bus speeds. The catalog also lists automated bike lane enforcement. Double parking gets its own product, aimed at a habit the company blames for crashes and lost time on transit routes. The platform is described as identifying objects rather than people.

Cities buy it for outcomes on bus routes, and the company frames the payoff as fewer collisions. Leadership comes from artificial intelligence, data science, transportation, and government technology. The company reports six GovTech 100 wins between 2021 and 2026.

paragraphs: Skydio makes autonomous drones, along with the docks and software to run them, and sells drone programs to customers from energy networks to neighborhood precincts to battlefields. Those programs cover Drone as First Responder, automated inspection and site security. Dock for X10 positions Skydio X10 drones at a site so that missions launch remotely without anyone present. The smaller Skydio R10 puts eyes indoors before officers enter.

Skydio states that more than 1,500 public safety agencies use its drones. In a Drone as First Responder program, Skydio says its drones launch in under 20 seconds and reach incidents autonomously in under 90 seconds. DFR Command is the software from which remote operators launch and manage drones, respond to multiple calls and stream live video to patrol and command. It integrates with RapidSOS and CAD at dispatch, Axon Fusus for live operations, and automatic evidence upload into Axon Evidence. Skydio's customer stories include Brookhaven PD, which it says reached 30 second response times after deploying 8 Docks.

Skydio Site Security uses the same dock-based drones to verify alarms, patrol perimeters and deliver live visibility across a site. Video streams into Genetec or Milestone, and flights launch automatically when triggered by alarms or access control events. Skydio says its data is encrypted in transit and at rest and that it aligns to SOC 2, ISO 27001 and NIST frameworks.

before.name: Citiri
before.description: CitiriOS owner scope management and operational readiness (ORAT) for transit, airports, and utilities

paragraphs: Citiri sells CitiriOS, a system owners use to define readiness, assign accountability, collect accepted evidence, and govern gate decisions. The company aims it at organizations launching complex infrastructure and services.

The premise is that finishing construction is not the same as being ready to operate. The discipline the company calls Owner Scope Management runs as a chain in which the owner defines what must be true to operate, evidence proves it, and gates authorize it. The output is a Ready Score along with accepted evidence and gate decisions. An agent named Opti surfaces false greens, aging blockers, and the decisions that still need an owner. People, not the software, approve every evidence and gate decision.

The company is direct about the boundary, saying CitiriOS is not a PMIS, commissioning tool, EAM/CMMS, document repository, or BI replacement. Citiri says it is helping the ATL team manage a $13B capital program that includes more than 114 distinct projects. It also describes the SFO team using CitiriOS to keep the Harvey Milk Terminal One project on track. A companion layer, OpsCenter, is listed as generally available, while an ecosystem orchestrator called Struxis is listed as limited access.

before.name: Via
before.description: On-demand transit, paratransit, and network planning software for agencies - exhibited at CTAA EXPO 2026

paragraphs: Via sells software and operating services for public transportation, working with the agencies and cities that run it. The company says it works with more than 700 partners around the world, from rural counties to large transit agencies.

Its on demand microtransit is pitched for first and last mile connections and for places with little transit service. For paratransit, the system optimizes routes and taps other accessible modes when they fit. An eligibility tool automates paratransit applications, approvals, and renewals. A planning product, Remix, is for visualizing data and testing network concepts before a redesign goes live. A student transit product provides scheduling and routing software meant to get every student to school on time.

Via also runs service itself under what it calls a transportation as a service model, rather than only supplying software. Its site carries comments from riders, mayors, agency leaders, planners, and dispatchers. A newer offering, Via Intelligence, is described as giving city and agency leaders recommendations and automations to lift efficiency and service performance.

paragraphs: Optibus sells an end-to-end, AI-powered platform for planning and operating more equitable, sustainable, and efficient public transportation. The site groups its buyers into authorities and cities, operators, shuttles, and consultancies.

One platform covers everything from planning and scheduling to real-time depot operations and sharing information with drivers and passengers. Planning tools let a team plan, analyze, and optimize a network to improve service quality and performance. The scheduling side creates optimal crew and vehicle schedules. Optibus Agent runs inside the platform, connected to real operational data and built around real workflows. That agent is included for all customers at no additional cost.

The company states that it is ISO 27001:2022 certified and SOC 2 compliant, using advanced encryption. It connects with existing CAD/AVL, HR/payroll, and on-board hardware. For electric fleets it offers tools that account for battery range, charging infrastructure, and grid constraints.

paragraphs: Axon sells public safety agencies a connected set of hardware and software: Axon Body 4 cameras, Axon Fleet 3 cameras, TASER 10 energy weapons and drones, unified on a real-time crime center platform with an open ecosystem of integrated partners. The company describes itself as an operating system for public safety. TASER 10, its current less-lethal weapon, can deploy up to 10 individually targeted probes without reloading when de-escalation fails.

Axon Fusus puts officer location, alerts, dispatch data, ALPR overlays and video feeds on a single live map so command, field and real-time crime center teams work from the same picture. Residents and businesses can opt in through Community Connect to share their camera video, and those cameras then appear on the Fusus map. The Axon AI Era Plan bundles current and future Axon AI products for a fixed annual cost. Among them is Draft One, which generates first-draft report narratives from audio transcripts of digital evidence and details the officer narrates. Axon Assistant, a voice assistant on the Body 4 camera, translates conversations when no human interpreter is available.

Chief Gary Berg of Campbell PD is quoted saying Fusus lets him see live location, alerts and video from body cams, drones and public safety cameras in one platform. Axon says it is on a mission to cut gun-related deaths between police and the public in half by 2033 through technology, training and trust.

before.name: Safety Vision
before.description: Mobile video surveillance and fleet safety cameras for mass transit, school buses, and police - exhibited at CTAA EXPO 2026, NAPT Summit 2026, SWANA WASTECON 2025
before.source: APTA 2026; NSA 2026; CTAA EXPO 2026; NAPT Summit 2026; SWANA WASTECON 2025
before.buyer: School districts are the largest named segment (700+ districts, 30M+ bus route miles); also mass transit agencies (25M+ commuters), EMS/emergency services, and commercial trucking

paragraphs: Safety Vision designs and delivers mobile video surveillance and fleet safety systems for organizations that run vehicles. The company says it designs, builds, installs and maintains solutions for virtually any mobile video surveillance application. Hardware spans recorders, interior and exterior cameras, monitors, sensors, battery backups and portable camera kits, alongside software for managing and viewing video.

The site groups the work by industry, listing student transportation, mass transit, public safety and commercial trucking. School districts get a platform meant to increase student safety both on and off the bus, and transit fleets get equipment protecting drivers, passengers and assets. For public safety, the pages say fire, EMS and law enforcement fleets use the mobile surveillance products, and commercial vehicle customers use them to protect trucks, drivers and assets.

Software includes SafetyNET 5, a video management system the company developed, and SafeDrive AI 2, a windshield camera and recorder combining driver assistance with driver behavior monitoring. A plugin for Milestone XProtect lets on-prem and mobile video surveillance be monitored in one place. The homepage states adherence to National Defense Authorization Act requirements in procurement and membership in the AWS Partner Network.

quote.text: SMARTER SOLUTIONS SUPPORT BETTER DECISIONS.

provenance.quote: Safety Vision designs and delivers AI-powered mobile video surveillance and fleet safety solutions that help fleet managers operate safely and efficiently.
We design, build, install and maintain solutions for virtually any mobile video surveillance application.
State-of-the-art sensors. Reliable battery backups. Safety Vision has everything you need to outfit your fleet.
Safety Vision has wide-ranging expertise in every application using mobile video surveillance solutions, from public sector to private business and beyond.
Our intelligent, expandable solutions allow for a single, integrated platform to increase student safety both on and off the bus.
Whether fire, EMS or law enforcement, first responders rely on our mobile surveillance solutions to help perform their duties safely.
SafeDrive AI 2 is an intelligent windshield Camera/ DVR that integrates the functions of an advanced driver assistance system (ADAS) and driver behavior monitoring into a single powerful solution.
With Safety Vision’s Milestone XProtect Plugin, you can monitor your on-prem and mobile video surveillance all in one place.

We fully adhere to the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) requirements in our procurement processes, providing our customers with reliable, compliant, and trusted mobile video surveillance solutions.

paragraphs: Motive sells fleet software and hardware as one integrated suite built around AI. The buyers are commercial fleets, which the company describes as ranging from five or ten vehicles up to companies running thousands of them.

On the safety side, cameras and AI flag more than twenty kinds of event on the road. High-confidence events go straight to managers, while a safety team reviews the low-confidence ones to remove false positives. Vehicle tracking uses real-time GPS with traffic updates and weather overlays for route planning. Compliance work such as electronic logs, driver qualification, IFTA and CSA sits in the same platform. Equipment monitoring shows what share of the time an asset is in use and how long it sits dormant. Telematics from various equipment manufacturers is centralized in a single platform.

The company points to operations running from waste services to construction. It says it was named number one in fleet management across every segment. It also cites top rankings for equipment monitoring in G2 asset tracking reports for summer 2026. Its fleet card is issued by Sutton Bank under a license from Mastercard International.

before.name: CSched
before.description: Transit scheduling consulting and exclusive North American HASTUS reseller (acquired by CIMA+, 2026)

paragraphs: CSched sells scheduling services and software tools to public transit agencies, private operators, and school boards, whatever their size or mode of transportation. The company is the exclusive authorized reseller of GIRO's HASTUS software in North America.

Its scheduling and operations modules are built on the HASTUS platform. When an agency is short of schedulers, its Rent-a-Scheduler service supplies coverage from the short term to the long term. Training runs from foundational courses to advanced HASTUS workshops. Consulting work covers efficiency audits, labor negotiations, and tender bids. The firm also advises agencies adapting their scheduling practices for the shift to electric buses.

Transit agencies worldwide have relied on CSched since 2008. The site says more than 4,650 buses run every day on schedules developed with its software or services. CSched calls itself the only consulting firm fully dedicated to public transit scheduling. It operates globally with a strong presence in North America, serving agencies, school boards, and private operators. Its experts are described as bringing over 100 years of combined hands-on experience.

before.name: Swiftly
before.description: Real-time transit data: arrival predictions and on-time performance

paragraphs: Swiftly sells a cloud platform to public transit agencies for sharing real-time passenger information, running daily operations, and improving service performance. The company puts its customer count above 200 agencies. Those agencies are described as large and small, around the globe.

The platform combines GTFS schedule data with whatever real-time vehicle location feed an agency already has. It then analyzes billions of data points to say where a vehicle was, where it is, and where it will be next. Operations staff use it to make real-time adjustments for on-time performance and headway adherence. Schedulers work from actual run times, vehicle speeds, and dwell times. APIs push the same data out to rider-facing apps, vehicle hardware, and internal tools.

Customer service teams are another audience, answering rider questions from the same information. The site carries comments from transit staff, including an operations technology lead at the MBTA in Boston. Another comes from a transportation planner at MDOT MTA in Baltimore. Jonny Simkin co-founded the company and is its chief executive. Swiftly describes itself as a transit reliability platform meant to keep public transportation a fast and attractive alternative to the private vehicle.

provenance.quote: Agencies rely on Swiftly’s cloud-native platform to share real-time passenger information, manage day-to-day operations, and improve service performance.
Trusted by 200+ agencies
Swiftly is improving public transit at agencies large and small around the globe.

Swiftly analyzes billions of data points to create the industry’s most accurate information about where a vehicle was, is, and where it will be next.
Boost on-time performance and headway adherence with real-time adjustments for your operators and historical insights for operations staff.
Optimize your schedule using actual run-times, vehicle speeds, and dwell times.
Swiftly's APIs make it simple to integrate with the entire transit ecosystem, including rider-facing apps, vehicle hardware, and internal tools.
your customer service team can instantly answer any question a rider has about your system
Dave Barker, Operations Technology | MBTA, Boston, MA

Jonny Simkin is the Co-founder and CEO of Swiftly.
Swiftly is a transit reliability platform to keep public transportation a fast, frequent, and attractive alternative to the private vehicle.

after.description: Real-time transit data: arrival predictions and on-time performance - exhibited at APTA 2026

paragraphs: Swiftly sells a cloud platform to public transit agencies for sharing real-time passenger information, running daily operations, and improving service performance. The company puts its customer count above 200 agencies. Those agencies are described as large and small, around the globe.

The platform combines GTFS schedule data with whatever real-time vehicle location feed an agency already has. It then analyzes billions of data points to say where a vehicle was, where it is, and where it will be next. Operations staff use it to make real-time adjustments for on-time performance and headway adherence. Schedulers work from actual run times, vehicle speeds, and dwell times. APIs push the same data out to rider-facing apps, vehicle hardware, and internal tools.

Customer service teams are another audience, answering rider questions from the same information. The site carries comments from transit staff, including an operations technology lead at the MBTA in Boston. Another comes from a transportation planner at MDOT MTA in Baltimore. Jonny Simkin co-founded the company and is its chief executive. Swiftly describes itself as a transit reliability platform meant to keep public transportation a fast and attractive alternative to the private vehicle.

paragraphs: Peak Transit sells fixed route transit software for agencies that need real-time vehicle tracking, transit dispatch tools, rider apps, and NTD reporting in one integrated platform. The platform covers CAD/AVL dispatch, in-vehicle operator tools, branded passenger apps, ridership data collection, ADA-compliant announcements, and real-time passenger information displays. Six tools share a unified data layer: CAD/AVL, MDTs, rider app, APC, AVAS, and digital signage.

paragraphs: INFODEV EDI develops and installs automatic passenger and people counting systems and has worked in this industry since 1993. The counting systems cover buses, trains, trams, subways, and railway and bus stations. Infodev EDI describes years of experience implementing automatic passenger counting projects in public transit. The home page describes ridership data for transit agencies that goes beyond basic passenger counts.

The DA-Series counting sensors are stated as accurate between 97.5% and 99.5%, at door level and without a correction factor. The DA-400 is a directional sensor that can be as thin as 13.5 mm for surface or inside-panel mounting above doors. The DA-200 is built to fit narrow doors and holds a single sensor in an aluminium case.

The GW-400 is a compact onboard counting computer that works with the DA-Series sensors to form an automatic passenger counting system. Data is usually transferred directly from the GW-400 via a wireless module to the ground data analysis server. INFODEV EDI also offers a software package alongside the counting hardware. Systems come in two architectures, a classical one that yields historical data for analysis and reporting and an enhanced one that yields real-time data.

quote.text: 97.5% to 99.5% Accuracy from Pure Counting Data in an Uncontrolled Transit Environment

before.name: Applied Information
before.description: Connected-vehicle ITS and the Glance smart-city platform: signal monitoring, preemption, school beacons - exhibited at IAFC FRI 2026

paragraphs: Applied Information makes traffic technology that turns intersections, school zones and connected vehicles into one real-time system. The customers are cities, which manage their traffic and ITS assets through a web-based application called Glance.

Glance monitors intersection cabinet equipment, reporting AC power, battery back up, cabinet flash, stop time, conflict monitor status, door switches, fan status and vehicle detectors. For emergency vehicles, an in-vehicle unit uses a cellular signal to tell the system a route has started. The system works out the route and talks wirelessly to the traffic cabinet to clear traffic ahead of the vehicle. School beacon flashers and their schedules can be viewed and controlled from anywhere. A connected vehicle product communicates over C-V2X, 4G LTE cellular and 900MHz.

The company states its hardware is designed, assembled and tested in Alpharetta, Georgia, with components meeting domestic content thresholds. A connected school bus system warns drivers approaching an active school safety zone or exceeding the speed limit. A smartphone app, Glance TravelSafely, extends the technology to residents.

quote.text: The drivers know they’ve got a green light in front of them, they know that everyone else has a red light, and they know the traffic is going to move ahead of them.

provenance.quote: Applied Information’s Glance® platform and smart-city solutions turn intersections, school zones, and connected vehicles into a unified, real-time system
allows cities to manage all their traffic and ITS assets under one, easy-to-use web-based application.
Data includes incoming AC power, battery back up, cabinet flash, stop time, conflict monitor status, door switches, fan status, vehicle detectors and more.
The moment a route starts, the in-vehicle unit uses a cellular signal to alert Glance of the emergency call.
Glance processes the route and communicates wirelessly with the traffic cabinet to clear traffic ahead of the vehicle’s arrival.

The Applied Information Connected Vehicle System simplifies and enables communication with C-V2X, 4G LTE cellular communication, and 900MHZ.

before.name: Littlepay
before.description: Contactless open-loop transit payment infrastructure for 400+ providers in 30+ countries

paragraphs: Littlepay sells payments infrastructure for transit, and public transit providers and vendors of all sizes use it to accept payments in person or online and simplify ticketing for passengers.

Open APIs allow flexible configuration of its capabilities alongside existing AFC and ABT fare collection systems. A single data platform gives operators visibility of passenger behaviour across vehicles, gates, kiosks, mobile apps and web. Risk models optimised across global volumes are meant to minimise losses from fraud and uncollected payments. Advanced PAN and PAR deny lists target card flipping fraud. Multi-operator brokerage services connect operators and agencies in a region under unified customer ticketing.

The company set out in 2016 with a vision to make contactless bank card acceptance faster, cheaper, and less complex for the public transit sector. It now describes working with over 400 transport and mobility providers in over 30 countries, powering payments on local buses, city networks and national public transport systems. One published case study describes Monterey-Salinas Transit deploying a contactless transit fare payment system in May 2021, the first of its kind in California.

quote.text: Why can a retail store set up a payment system in a matter of minutes for a few hundred dollars, while transit agencies take years and spend millions of dollars to do essentially the same thing?

before.name: Genfare
before.description: Fareboxes, validators, TVMs, and Genfare Link cloud fare software for 400+ NA transit agencies (SPX)

paragraphs: Genfare sells fare collection systems to public transit agencies, and describes itself as a partner to transit agencies of every size across the United States and Canada for more than forty years. Its systems cover fixed route service, microtransit, paratransit, ferries, and light rail.

The company is moving its Genfare Link platform to a fully cloud-based software-as-a-service model. Transaction, ridership, and device monitoring data from fareboxes, mobile apps, e-Fare portals, and retail channels are consolidated in one central location. For riders paying with a contactless bank card or phone, existing Fast Fare fareboxes can be upgraded for open payment, or an Open Link validator can be mounted next to the farebox. The Mobile Link application and the e-Fare online ticketing system use open APIs to work with microtransit and shared ride providers.

Genfare Link is built on Amazon Web Services, with APIs linking agency platforms to each other and to riders. Alongside the hardware and software, the company sells packages for training, maintenance and repair, and technical support.

paragraphs: SignAgent sells software for managing signs across built environments, described on its site as a single source of truth for every sign an operator owns. Through its three distinct interfaces, the platform covers design and planning, fabrication and installation, and ongoing management of signage and wayfinding. SignAgent Design is aimed at sign programming, with the stated aim of removing repetitive tasks, reducing costly errors, and speeding project delivery.

SignAgent Build and SignAgent Mobile cover order fulfillment, progress tracking, and completing installations. SignAgent Manage covers asset tracking, information updates, and cost management against sign standards over the long term. A phone and tablet app is listed for field work such as sign surveys, punch lists, and sign installation.

The spaces listed on the home page include Airports, Hospitals, Transit Systems, Higher Education, and Parks & Municipalities. Case studies name Metra Rail, Denver International Airport, and University of Chicago Medicine among clients. Alongside those operators, the site markets a vendor program to signage and wayfinding firms and to fabricators.

before.name: Beep
before.description: Turnkey autonomous shuttle operations for transit agencies, airports, and communities

paragraphs: Beep plans, deploys and manages autonomous shuttles for private and public communities. The services answer demand for alternative modes of transportation within communities, campuses and municipalities. Routes run inside geo-fenced areas at a controlled speed.

Deployments are built around first and last-mile trips, linking retail to residential areas, remote parking to campus amenities, and underserved communities to transit stops and stations. The service portfolio runs from upfront analysis, planning and design through turnkey operation of an autonomous mobility network. Underneath sits AutonomOS, a vehicle-agnostic platform for multi-passenger autonomous mobility services. It plans service modes from fixed route to demand-responsive variants. In-cabin monitoring built on machine learning lets remote supervisors react to a passenger safety or roadway issue.

The platform is built for public transit operators and authorities. The company reports deployments in six states and two dozen deployments overall. The purpose-built shuttles carry ADA-compliant wheelchair ramps and restraints. One announced project, ATL Spoke, is a pilot with Atlanta Beltline that the company says is in service and open to the public.

before.name: Cylus
before.description: CylusOne rail OT cybersecurity: threat detection for signaling, trackside, and onboard networks

paragraphs: Cylus makes cybersecurity software for railways, built to continuously monitor, detect, and protect every layer of rail operational technology. Its product, CylusOne, covers mainline, urban, and freight rail operations.

The system integrates passively into an operator's network and existing monitoring tools. It automatically discovers and classifies all assets in the operational networks. Vulnerabilities are prioritized and scored by analyzing their severity in the rail environment. Detection runs continuously using deep packet inspection and machine learning to identify and classify threats across railway and IT protocols. Coverage reaches trackside and wayside networks, train-to-ground communications, operational control and maintenance centers, and station networks.

The company says the product lets operators prove compliance with frameworks including IEC 62443-3-2, NIST 800-82, and EN TS 50701. It describes CylusOne as the first rail cybersecurity solution certified to IEC 62443-4-2 at Security Level 3. Cylus says it works with technology providers, integrators, and rail experts worldwide. For passenger rail, detection is tuned to separate expected supervision and control traffic in ERTMS environments from anomalous behavior.

quote.text: CylusOne enables teams to investigate and contain threats without disrupting service, integrates with existing SOC processes, and keeps freight rail operations at the center of decision-making.

paragraphs: INIT is a supplier of IT solutions for public transport, selling to operators around the world. Its systems cover all operational processes within a fully integrated ITS system.

Planning tools run from timetables through optimizing deployments to managing vehicles and drivers. Fare products handle smartcards, mobile tickets, ID- or account-based ticketing and Open Payment. Operations control covers monitoring the traffic situation, punctuality, disruption handling and passenger information. Transport companies can also use it for electromobility requirements and to set up a single sign-on mobility platform.

before.name: IVU Traffic Technologies
before.description: IVU.suite planning, scheduling, dispatch, and ticketing for transit and rail operators

paragraphs: IVU develops integrated IT systems for public transport, and says it has done so for more than fifty years. The customers are bus and rail operators of any size, from five vehicles to fifty and from two routes to two hundred. Its product, IVU.suite, covers planning, dispatch, fleet management, ticketing, passenger information and the settlement of transport contracts.

Timetabling runs from setting up route networks to publishing services and supplying operation control and passenger information systems. Vehicle scheduling is handled by IVU.run, which supports the entire schedule planning process. Duty scheduling merges thousands of duty elements, crewing guidelines and qualifications through optimisation algorithms. For electric fleets the system weighs charging times, ranges, route lengths and depot or opportunity charging. In daily operation it monitors vehicle status, the timetable situation and the current deployment of vehicles and staff. The whole suite is also offered as a hosted service.

The company says more than 500 customers worldwide use the standard products of the suite. Named deployments include the Lagos Metropolitan Area Transport Authority. It reports as IVU Traffic Technologies AG and has published preliminary results for the first half of 2026.

before.name: Basemap
before.description: TRACC travel-time and accessibility analysis plus transport datasets for government transport agencies

paragraphs: Basemap describes itself as an expert in transport software and data for accurate travel analysis. Its main product, TRACC, analyses travel times, optimises transit routes, and identifies accessibility gaps to key destinations. Government departments, city planners, transport operators, and consultants are named as the people who rely on those products.

Alongside the software, the company produces public transport timetables, average speed, and speed limit data for government agencies. DataCutter handles data management, with extraction tailored to a specific project. An electric vehicle routing product plans routes and forecasts energy consumption using more than 12 factors. Highways Analyst covers traffic data visualisation and analysis.

The case studies list the UK Department for Transport, which has been developing and publishing journey time statistics for over 10 years. Another describes OC Transpo, the municipal transit provider in Ottawa, starting to use TRACC for route and level of service planning. Leicestershire Tri-Service Fire and Rescue is described using Basemap speed datasets in its command and control system. An NHS case study covers a travel time analysis spanning emergency vehicles and private and public transport.

paragraphs: LiveView Technologies, known as LVT, sells rapidly deployable security units configured as mobile trailers, wall mounts, or pole mounts. The company says the units are used by DOTs, oil and gas operators, law enforcement, retailers, construction firms, and housing operators. Each mobile unit runs on its own, carrying solar panels, cellular and available satellite connectivity, lighting, a loud speaker, and a configurable selection of cameras. Pole-mounted versions instead take grid power for fixed coverage where infrastructure already exists.

The software side is a cloud platform reached from a phone or desktop, with a forensic search that sorts footage by keywords such as white car or crowd formation. From a mobile device an operator can zoom in, turn on the lights, and start speaker talk downs. A companion app called SafeNow lets employees set off floodlights, strobes, and audio warnings with one swipe.

On the public side, LVT lists remote monitoring of borders, government buildings, parks, school campuses, healthcare facilities, and military sites. The Arcadia Police Department added LVT Units to its operations for surveillance and crime prevention. Prologis put more than 70 LVT Units across industrial real estate properties in multiple states. LVT has been headquartered in Utah since 2005.

before.name: Archistar
before.description: AI planning and building code assessment tools sold to councils and cities

paragraphs: Archistar sells AI plan review software to local governments, with a product called AI PreCheck that speeds building code and zoning compliance checks so permits can be issued faster. The same platform is offered to developers, architects and certifiers, who can check compliance before submitting to a municipality or council.

Submitters drag and drop design files onto the platform, which accepts PDF, CAD or BIM formats and reviews them in 2D or 3D. The software then evaluates each submission against the city's local codes and regulations. It is built on generative AI, computer vision and machine learning. Applicants receive standardized reports. For municipalities and councils with particular zoning, planning and compliance requirements, tailored and white-labeled versions are offered.

The company says Archistar was founded by Dr. Benjamin Coorey in 2010 and began life as an education portal. It grew from a university research project into a platform that could read planning rules, run feasibility tests and generate compliant designs in minutes. The site states that Archistar powers digital planning for over 30 cities and governments across Australia, Canada and the United States. Among the municipalities it names supporting are LA County, the City of Los Angeles, the City of Austin and the City of New York. Offices are listed across Los Angeles, Vancouver and Sydney.

quote.text: What once took weeks of back-and-forth can now happen in seconds.

Applicants receive standardized reports. For municipalities and councils with particular zoning, planning and compliance requirements, tailored and white-labeled versions are offered.

The company says Archistar was founded by Dr. Benjamin Coorey in 2010 and began life as an education portal. It grew from a university research project into a platform that could read planning rules, run feasibility tests and generate compliant designs in minutes. The site states that Archistar powers digital planning for over 30 cities and governments across Australia, Canada and the United States. Among the municipalities it names supporting are LA County, the City of Los Angeles, the City of Austin and the City of New York. Offices are listed across Los Angeles, Vancouver and Sydney.

paragraphs: AchieveIt sells software for moving a written plan into measurable progress. It pitches itself to public agencies and other organizations that find performance hard to measure. The idea behind it is connecting people, plans and data in one place.

paragraphs: Apptegy sells a communications platform to K-12 school districts, gathering the tools and training that district staff use to reach families. The pitch to district leaders is that the school brand stays at the front of every message.

Districts get a branded website managed through a drag-and-drop editor with page permissions for contributors and analytics. A district-branded mobile app for iOS and Android carries school information and two-way messaging for families. Alerts go out by email, push notification, SMS, text-to-speech, voice call and social media from one place. Automated translation is offered for more than 100 languages, and websites are built to meet WCAG 2.1 A and AA standards.

The home page states that 5,273 districts have switched to the platform for their communications. Beyond software the company publishes SchoolCEO magazine, with guides and original research for district leaders. One study listed there was done jointly with NSPRA on the relationship between superintendents and school communicators.

before.name: Avolve Software
before.description: ProjectDox electronic plan review for building, fire, planning, and public works agencies

paragraphs: Avolve sells electronic plan review software to state and local government agencies. The product agencies implement for that work is ProjectDox. Customers quoted on the site also name a second product, DigEplan.

The software carries a review from the applicant's submission through to completion. Avolve describes the plan review as having GIS, AI and field mobility embedded. It is meant to fit whatever permitting stack an agency already runs. In a published case study, a water and sewer commission reviews about 3,500 plan submittals and 34,000 permit transactions a year. After implementing ProjectDox, that agency reported review times falling from eight weeks to two or three.

That commission serves more than 1.9 million people. Avolve says its plan review is built on insight from more than 350 government customers. Testimonials on its site come from cities and counties, including one crediting ProjectDox with improving operations across Minneapolis.

before.name: Accela
before.description: Permitting, licensing, and code enforcement platform for state and local government - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026
before.source: ICMA 2025; NRPA 2026; ICMA 2026; NLC City Summit 2026

paragraphs: Accela sells software that government agencies use to run permitting, licensing, and asset management from a single system. Its applications are built for individual government service workflows and can operate together or be deployed only where an agency needs them.

For building departments, intake, plan review, inspections, and permit issuance sit in one workflow rather than in separate disconnected steps. Reviewers from different departments work the same record at once, with annotations and approvals tracked as they happen. Planning teams get the same shared review model, plus automated public notice generation, hearing schedules, and agency notifications. Applicants can see where a case stands and receive consolidated feedback from every reviewing department.

The company says it has thirty years of government expertise built into the product. Testimonials on the site are attributed to municipal staff, including a chief building official in McAllen, Texas. Residents and businesses who encounter Accela through a local agency are directed to that agency rather than to the company.

paragraphs: Catalis sells software and payment services to government agencies. One line covers tax and CAMA work, supporting local billing, collection and management alongside appraisal and assessing. Another handles courts and land records, automating filings and widening public access to justice.

On the resident-facing side, the company offers municipalities a package covering website design, development, hosting and maintenance. Its notification tool distributes messages by email, text, social media and voice phone lines. Administrators can also automate alerts drawn from Alert Ready, NOAA and IPAWS. Permitting and licensing tools let residents apply online and route the reviews to staff.

The stated customer base spans municipalities, counties, states and federal agencies. The website design team says it has been doing this work since 1999. It claims more than 1,000 municipal websites built to date. The notification platform is described as incorporating 20 years of municipal experience.
