before.description: Connected-vehicle ITS and the Glance smart-city platform: signal monitoring, preemption, school beacons - exhibited at IAFC FRI 2026, APTA 2026

paragraphs: Applied Information makes traffic technology that turns intersections, school zones and connected vehicles into one real-time system. The customers are cities, which manage their traffic and ITS assets through a web-based application called Glance.

Glance monitors intersection cabinet equipment, reporting AC power, battery back up, cabinet flash, stop time, conflict monitor status, door switches, fan status and vehicle detectors. For emergency vehicles, an in-vehicle unit uses a cellular signal to tell the system a route has started. The system works out the route and talks wirelessly to the traffic cabinet to clear traffic ahead of the vehicle. School beacon flashers and their schedules can be viewed and controlled from anywhere. A connected vehicle product communicates over C-V2X, 4G LTE cellular and 900MHz.

The company states its hardware is designed, assembled and tested in Alpharetta, Georgia, with components meeting domestic content thresholds. A connected school bus system warns drivers approaching an active school safety zone or exceeding the speed limit. A smartphone app, Glance TravelSafely, extends the technology to residents.

quote.text: The drivers know they’ve got a green light in front of them, they know that everyone else has a red light, and they know the traffic is going to move ahead of them.

paragraphs: Applied Information makes traffic technology that turns intersections, school zones and connected vehicles into one real-time system. The customers are cities, which manage their traffic and ITS assets through a web-based application called Glance.

Glance monitors intersection cabinet equipment, reporting AC power, battery back up, cabinet flash, stop time, conflict monitor status, door switches, fan status and vehicle detectors. For emergency vehicles, an in-vehicle unit uses a cellular signal to tell the system a route has started. The system works out the route and talks wirelessly to the traffic cabinet to clear traffic ahead of the vehicle. School beacon flashers and their schedules can be viewed and controlled from anywhere. A connected vehicle product communicates over C-V2X, 4G LTE cellular and 900MHz.

The company states its hardware is designed, assembled and tested in Alpharetta, Georgia, with components meeting domestic content thresholds. A connected school bus system warns drivers approaching an active school safety zone or exceeding the speed limit. A smartphone app, Glance TravelSafely, extends the technology to residents.

quote.text: The drivers know they’ve got a green light in front of them, they know that everyone else has a red light, and they know the traffic is going to move ahead of them.

before.name: BusPatrol
before.description: School bus stop-arm cameras with violator-funded safety programs

paragraphs: BusPatrol runs school bus stop-arm enforcement programs alongside school districts, municipalities, and law enforcement agencies. The company says communities can enforce the law around stopped buses at no upfront cost.

Cameras on the bus detect illegal passings and capture video evidence of them. Agencies review the results through dashboards, monthly reports, and compliance tools. The program also runs public awareness and public service campaigns meant to change how drivers behave.

BusPatrol states that it partners with school districts in 26 states. It says communities using the program see measurable reductions in dangerous driving around stopped school buses. The company traces its origin to a child killed while getting off his school bus in Ontario, Canada. Its staff, by its own description, includes technologists, retired police officers, and teachers.

before.name: Acapela Group
before.description: Text-to-speech voice software - exhibited at APTA 2026

paragraphs: Acapela Group sells text-to-speech software that turns written service information into spoken announcements. The transport work spans rail, urban transport, airports and automotive systems.

Voices are tuned for train stations, bus stops, metro and tram systems, and pronunciation can be corrected in a lexicon editor. Deployment can be in the cloud, embedded in a device, or hybrid, on Linux, Android, iOS and Windows. A server edition speech-enables telecommunications applications and server-based services in real time. Development kits are sold per platform, including one for Linux applications.

The transport page shows a custom voice built for BVG, the Berlin public transport operator. Another sample is a custom voice for Transport for London. The company states GDPR compliance and offers on-device or offline processing.

before.name: Blyncsy
before.description: AI detection of pavement markings and road defects from crowdsourced dashcams (Bentley Systems)

paragraphs: Blyncsy helps cities and state departments of transportation automate their roadway maintenance and asset inventory activities. Rather than sending crews out to look, it works from crowd-sourced dash camera imagery.

Machine learning algorithms and image processing applied to that imagery detect where and when pavement needs maintenance. Condition assessments run from pot holes to paint striping and crosswalk conditions. Paint lines are rated from 1, the worst, to 5, the best. In construction zones the same imagery detects work zone equipment to put those zones on the map. Those detections can also check whether a maintenance of traffic plan matches reality. A further model detects the presence of debris on and beside the road. The AI also estimates the size of the debris it finds.

Results are delivered directly into OpenGIS or another preferred platform. The company claims savings of up to 90% compared to traditional manual inspections. It puts the cost at $10 per centerline mile against $200 or more for a LiDAR scan. News items on the site include a City of Fort Worth partnership on the first phase of automated asset inventory. Another announces a sustainability partner designation in the Google Cloud Partner Advantage Program.

before.name: Acusensus
before.description: AI cameras detecting phone use, seatbelt, and speed violations for road authorities

paragraphs: Acusensus sells automated traffic enforcement systems to the road authorities and police agencies that are trying to cut deaths and injuries on the road network. Its main product, Heads-Up, detects drivers illegally using a mobile phone and captures evidence intended to stand up in a prosecution.

The same camera pass picks up other behaviours, so one deployment can address seatbelt non-compliance and speed measured at a point or averaged over a distance. A companion product sends live alerts to officers working the roadside. Assessment happens at the roadside, and images of drivers who are not offending are discarded almost immediately. Evidence that is kept is encrypted so that only the customer agency can open it.

The company says the government of New South Wales used its technology in a program enforcing against illegal phone use by drivers. Its list of delivered work includes an Arkansas speed enforcement program covering work zones. Acusensus also reports ISO accreditation for occupational health and safety, quality, environmental and information security management systems.

quote.text: Acusensus provides advanced traffic enforcement solutions to change behaviours and prevent road trauma.

provenance.quote: Acusensus provides advanced traffic enforcement solutions to change behaviours and prevent road trauma.
Acusensus Heads-Up uses patented technology to detect and capture prosecutable evidence of drivers illegally using mobile phones whilst driving.
The solution additionally simultaneously captures evidence of other dangerous driver behaviours including seatbelt non-compliance and speeding (at a point or averaged over a distance).
Acusensus Real-Time provides alerts to police officers of drivers using a phone, speeding, not wearing a seatbelt or on an automatic number plate recognition wanted list.
data for non offending drivers is deleted in near real-time by the roadside
Evidence captured by Acusensus solutions is envelope encrypted such that only end customers can decrypt and view the data
Acusensus technology was used by the government of New South Wales, Australia in their world first program to enforce against illegal mobile phone use by drivers.
Arkansas Speed Enforcement Program using Harmony Real Time in work zones

Acusensus received ISO accreditation for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems (45001:2018); Quality Management Systems (9001:2015); Environmental Management Systems (14001:2015); and Information Security Management Systems (ISO/IEC 27001:2022).

before.name: DeepWalk
before.description: iPhone-lidar sidewalk and curb-ramp inspection for ADA transition plans, ArcGIS-integrated; 120+ munis

paragraphs: DeepWalk sells automated sidewalk inspection software that uses iPhone LiDAR to identify condition and access issues. Work is planned, inspected, analyzed and implemented on one platform. Projects range from small residential work to city-wide deployments.

Crews scan sidewalk and curb ramps with the LiDAR scanners in iPhone Pros through the mobile app. An automated measurement system then inspects the scans for condition and accessibility issues. Data comes back in the web app and in ArcGIS. There, inspections are managed, conditions reviewed and work orders created for improvements. A higher plan is aimed at large evaluations and long-term planning projects that require slope analysis.

All plans include the full capability of the mobile app, which is downloaded from the Apple App Store. The site describes a pilot in which Edina, MN, got faster, more efficient data collection. Another story says Genoa, IL, went from data collection to program implementation and earned statewide recognition.

before.name: Palo Alto Networks
before.description: Cybersecurity software and network security platforms - exhibited at IACP 2026, NASCIO 2026, CoSN 2026, EDUCAUSE 2026

paragraphs: Palo Alto Networks sells cybersecurity products across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. The company says more than 70,000 customers use them, backed by its Unit 42 threat intelligence group.

Its network security platform monitors, analyzes and prevents sophisticated threats in real time with less complexity. An identity platform adds a control plane that discovers risk, applies privilege dynamically and governs access from first session to last. In a May 2026 release the company announced it had closed its acquisition of Portkey, described as a pioneer in AI gateways. That gateway watches token usage against runaway costs and adds runtime protection against malicious or unintended AI behavior.

Customer stories are filed by industry, and state and local government is one of the categories. One story describes VINCI standardising on Cortex XDR across 200,000 endpoints worldwide. The company runs executive briefing centers where customers meet its executives and product leaders. Briefings run from half a day to several days and are tailored to the visiting organization. Palo Alto Networks is listed on the Nasdaq under PANW.

paragraphs: Beep plans, deploys and manages autonomous shuttles for private and public communities. The services answer demand for alternative modes of transportation within communities, campuses and municipalities. Routes run inside geo-fenced areas at a controlled speed.

Deployments are built around first and last-mile trips, linking retail to residential areas, remote parking to campus amenities, and underserved communities to transit stops and stations. The service portfolio runs from upfront analysis, planning and design through turnkey operation of an autonomous mobility network. Underneath sits AutonomOS, a vehicle-agnostic platform for multi-passenger autonomous mobility services. It plans service modes from fixed route to demand-responsive variants. In-cabin monitoring built on machine learning lets remote supervisors react to a passenger safety or roadway issue.

The platform is built for public transit operators and authorities. The company reports deployments in six states and two dozen deployments overall. The purpose-built shuttles carry ADA-compliant wheelchair ramps and restraints. One announced project, ATL Spoke, is a pilot with Atlanta Beltline that the company says is in service and open to the public.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "AWS is the world's most comprehensive cloud, enabling organizations to accelerate innovation, reduce costs, and scale more efficiently" The URL is factually correct and does NOT violate the parent-domain rule: aws.amazon.com is AWS's own canonical property (its own brand, console, pricing, docs and its own careers page at https://aws.amazon.com/careers/, HTTP 200), not Amazon's corporate site at amazon.com. The govtech tie is on-domain too: https://aws.amazon.com/government-education/ (HTTP 200) is AWS's public sector page, and the homepage names 'AWS GovCloud (US-East)' and 'AWS GovCloud (US-West)'. MY JUDGMENT ON WHETHER THE BOARD SHOULD CARRY THIS AT ALL - the URL passes but the record is still risky, for a reason the URL check cannot fix: aws.amazon.com/careers/ does not host jobs, it hands off to https://www.amazon.jobs/en/business_categories/amazon-web-services. That feed is tens of thousands of global AWS engineering/PM/ops roles, of which SLED account executive roles are a tiny fraction. Any homepage- or careers-page-level scrape of this record will flood SLED JOBS with irrelevant listings - the same practical damage the parent-domain rule exists to prevent, arriving by a different route. Recommendation: keep the URL if AWS is wanted on the board, but the record must be wired to

before.name: HAAS Alert
before.description: Safety Cloud digital alerting for DOT, fire and public works fleets - exhibited at IAFC FRI 2026

paragraphs: HAAS Alert sells a collision prevention service that sends real-time digital alerts warning drivers about nearby emergency vehicles and roadway hazards. Its customers are fleets that work at the roadside, including tow trucks, utility vehicles, waste management trucks, school buses and snowplows.

The system is wired to a vehicle's warning light bar or master switch, so alerting begins when crews turn on their lights and stops when they turn them off. Motorists install nothing, because alerts are broadcast directly to the navigation platforms they already use. Fleets can activate the service through three primary methods, depending on their existing setup. The company says drivers get up to 30 seconds of advance warning to slow down and move over.

The company traces its start to 2015, when co-founder and CEO Cory Hohs was almost struck by an ambulance on the road. He co-founded the business with Noah Levens and Jigar Patel. Its timeline notes that the United States Department of Homeland Security awarded $1.1 million toward development for digital alerting. It also states that digital alerting was codified and funded in the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.

before.name: Compass IoT
before.description: Connected-vehicle road safety and network analytics for road authorities

paragraphs: Compass IoT sells connected vehicle data for road networks, taken from the cars themselves rather than roadside equipment or phones. The company says more than 3,000 users globally use its connected vehicle data to understand traffic across their road networks. Its Road Intelligence platform presents that network-wide vehicle data in a browser.

The data comes from cloud-connected vehicles that have an internet connection. Compass says it receives over a billion connected vehicle data points every day from 64 different car manufacturers. Each record can carry location, timestamp, speed, acceleration, make and model, plus road attributes such as the speed limit and pavement type. Coverage runs across virtually every road in Australia.

Published case studies show clients using the tools for road safety, city planning, and infrastructure questions. One covers Sunshine Coast Council measuring how speed cushions retrofitted at a pedestrian crossing changed driver behaviour. Afterwards, average speed in both directions dropped to 22km/h. Another describes the Inner West Council using data-driven evidence to lower speed limits for pedestrian and cyclist safety. Compass IoT UK has received funding from EIT Urban Mobility as part of the third SME Expansion Open Call.

paragraphs: Ellucian sells administrative software to colleges and universities, covering the student lifecycle alongside finance and human capital management. The catalog is organized around student information systems, human capital management, and finance and operations.

The student product is presented as covering the whole lifecycle, from first inquiry through graduation. before.name: Meadow
before.description: Student billing, payments, net price calculator, and pre-collections software for colleges and universities - exhibited at NACUBO 2026

paragraphs: Meadow makes software that handles the student financial experience at colleges, from application to graduation. The company says more than 300 higher education institutions use it.

One product is a net price calculator that gives prospective students a cost estimate in under three minutes. A billing product aims to cut manual work for staff and resolve balances sooner. A pre-collections product goes after unpaid tuition balances without punitive action. A checkout product collects non-tuition payments such as parking passes, lab fees, event costs and ID replacements.

One case study follows Tulsa Community College, which implemented the pre-collections product. The gap it addressed was the six-month period between the end of a semester and referral to traditional collections. Text messaging proved especially effective there for the college's dual enrollment population. Meadow also joined a Foundation for California Community Colleges procurement program to widen access to its tools among California community colleges and independent institutions. The founders trace the idea back to a bad higher education financial experience of their own.

before.description: Cloud permitting, licensing, code enforcement, and GIS workflows for local governments - exhibited at GFOA 2026

paragraphs: GovPilot sells cloud-based management software to municipal and county government departments. The pitch is to put a government's data and its departments on a single platform. Local governments of all sizes have deployed it.

A government picks the modules it needs, then unifies data across departments and lets residents report concerns, apply, pay and track requests online. The catalog runs to more than 125 templated digital modules, with mobile apps and a GIS map on the same cloud platform. A parcel-level view called PropertyProfile shows records held by different departments about the same property. Two mobile apps, GovAlert and GovInspect, accompany the digital forms and automated workflows.

Case studies on the site cover work such as building and construction permitting. Short-term rental property registration is another documented use. Pricing is set by population and by the number of modules a government selects. The company says it has been named a GovTech 100 company for eight consecutive years. It also points buyers to its Capterra reviews from government users.

paragraphs: Geotab sells fleet management technology that commercial vehicle operators use to track vehicles and run their operations from one system. The company describes what it offers as an open platform for safe, sustainable and cost-effective mobility powered by AI and data intelligence. Video safety is part of the same package, with dash cameras feeding into the MyGeotab software.

The GO tracking device plugs into a vehicle's onboard diagnostics port. Once driving begins it records location, speed, engine idling and distance. Dash cam footage and alert data upload to the cloud so managers can review video later. An analytics layer standardizes data from every vehicle source and enriches it with context such as road conditions, driver history and maintenance records. Developers can extend the platform with sample code and custom add-in pages.

Police and first responders are among the industries the site lists. Geotab reports more than six million connected vehicles. It also claims 26 years of fleet expertise. The company states that the platform is backed by ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II certifications and that its AI aligns with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. Support is described as staffed around the clock by experts who are in-market rather than offshored.

before.name: Bytecurve
before.description: School bus operations, driver pay and dispatch software for districts

paragraphs: Bytecurve sells operations software for school bus fleets, tying routing and GPS data into driver management, dispatching and payroll. The company pitches its payroll application as one that catches pay inconsistencies, and says it was built by people who worked in K12 transportation. Private student transportation contractors are one audience for it, and school districts are the other.

Real-time integration with routing systems and GPS lets dispatchers reassign drivers on the fly and break routes apart. Time and attendance removes manual calculation of employee guarantees, contracts and overtime, and runs through a mobile app or a garage-based tablet. Drivers check in and out remotely, view schedules and receive messages on their phones. Dispatchers get immediate alerts for late or missing drivers, and access to the driver app is limited to authorized employees through a customer-specific code.

The company says dozens of districts use the system across more than 40,000 buses and 50,000 drivers. Its founders claim over 30 years of combined transportation experience, with a focus on student transportation. One case study states that Rome Public Schools reduced payroll by $30,000 per month.

paragraphs: Flock Safety sells license plate readers, video cameras, gunshot detection and response drones to law enforcement agencies, schools, businesses and neighborhoods to help them deter crime, respond to emergencies and investigate safety incidents. Its license plate recognition cameras capture plates and vehicle characteristics such as make, color and body type to generate investigative leads. Responders get an instant alert when a vehicle matches a customer-defined or NCIC hot list. Users include law enforcement agencies, businesses, neighborhoods, apartment complexes, houses of worship and schools.

Beyond plate readers, Flock sells PTZ video cameras for open areas such as parking lots, intersections and parks, and fixed cameras for buildings and city streets. A gunshot and audio detection product verifies gunfire and links each alert with nearby LPR reads and video. Flock DFR, its drone as first responder system, launches a docked drone to the coordinates of a 911 call, LPR hit or gunshot alert and streams live video to officers before they arrive. Solar-powered mobile trailers cover parking lots, retail centers and construction sites, and an optional Alert Response Service puts trained agents on live alerts.

Flock sells on an annual subscription that covers hardware, software, maintenance and support. The company has reduced its recommended default data retention from 30 days to 7 days, which it says applies to new law enforcement customers. Customers control their data and how it is shared, and every search is logged.

Our "Police" category captures their largest and most visible segment and is fair, but be aware roughly half their published industry pages are commercial; if the board ever filters on "government-only vendors," Flock should not be in that bucket.

Veritone Redact automates face and audio redaction of bodycam footage for the same agency FOIA/records staff

paragraphs: Pimloc sells Secure Redact, an automated system for the bulk redaction of personal data from video. It is aimed at private and public organizations that want to automate data privacy compliance while still getting operational value from their video. Customers use it to process video for data subject access requests and freedom of information requests.

The system's models recognize identifiers such as faces, heads and license plates the way a human observer would, then redact and classify them automatically. It can be applied selectively, removing some or all faces or all vehicle registration details, and it is trained to perform on low-definition CCTV footage. Pimloc states that Secure Redact detects and anonymizes over 99% of identifiable PII in security video. It also says redaction with its AI runs 200 times faster than doing the job by hand.

The company says its capabilities are deployed across transport, public safety, telehealth, insurance, retail, policing and local government. A second product, Pholio, classifies visual content, and Pimloc has used it to evaluate automated detection of online harms. Founders Simon Randall, the CEO, and James Leigh, the CTO, co-created the Autographer wearable image capture device at a previous business, and the privacy challenges of always-on capture led them to start Pimloc.

quote.text: Automated anonymization is the only way to keep up with changing privacy legislation and to responsibly unlock the value of aggregated video data for business operations.

Pimloc is helping private and public organizations across the globe to automate data privacy compliance whilst responsibly unlocking the operational value of multi-modal data intelligence.

before.name: ClearGov
before.description: Budget building and transparency software for local governments and schools - exhibited at GFOA 2026

paragraphs: ClearGov sells cloud-based software that local governments and school districts use to manage the finance cycle, and it counts more than 2,000 of them as users. Published documents are a large part of the job, with budget books, ACFRs, PAFRs, annual reports, and CIP books built from guided templates.

Department heads submit capital requests through web-based forms that collect consistent data and feed a central dashboard. Finance staff can build and compare different budget scenarios before settling on a plan. Approved work can be published to automatically updated Public Project Pages carrying timelines, financials, maps, photos, and announcements. A strategic plan can likewise be turned into a website so constituents can follow progress over time. Outputs are generated ADA-compliant for sharing, publishing, or print-ready PDF distribution.

The company reports $540B in managed budgets. It also cites a 98% customer satisfaction figure. Its customer success team includes former local government finance officers. For counties, a built-in checklist maps to the criteria for the NACo EDGE Excellence in Strategic Planning Award.

before.name: TCP Software
before.description: Time, attendance and scheduling for government, education and public safety - exhibited at GFOA 2026

paragraphs: TCP Software sells scheduling, time, and attendance solutions to organizations of any size or sector. The range covers automated time and attendance, employee scheduling, time clock hardware, and integrations for ERP, HCM, and payroll systems. TimeClock Plus covers time tracking, leave and accrual management, and K-12 resource management.

Humanity Schedule builds and adjusts shifts automatically, using AI to forecast demand and match qualified staff to shifts. It connects to payroll, ERP, or HCM software from providers including ADP, Oracle, Workday, and BambooHR, or through an open API. Humanity Time is offered to smaller teams for tracking time, attendance, and labor costs.

Aladtec is the public safety product, sold for 24/7 rotational scheduling to fire, EMS, law enforcement, and corrections agencies. Its schedules carry work, union, and fatigue rules so that an agency can answer an audit.

quote.text: 24/7 automated staff scheduling built for the unique rotation patterns and union policies of public safety and government agencies.

paragraphs: Workday sells cloud software that runs human resources, finance and IT processes for an organization. Its human capital management line is a suite of HR products meant to work as one. The company says the software is built for organizations of all sizes. A packaged version is aimed at midsize businesses.

Inside the HR suite sit time tracking, absence, scheduling and payroll. Payroll is automated to pay workers accurately and in line with local rules. Recruiting covers the full talent acquisition lifecycle. The company argues the value comes from a single data model and one codeline rather than systems stitched together. It claims native localization for more than 175 countries.

More than 10,000 organizations use Workday, including a majority of the Fortune 500 by the company's own count. Customer stories on the site include Panera. Workday also cites Gartner recognition for cloud HCM suites.

paragraphs: Durham School Services runs contracted student transportation for school districts across the country. The company describes itself as part of a network that carries more than a million students every day.

A district that contracts with Durham hands over routing, fleet, staffing and maintenance. Beyond daily routes, the company offers specialized service designed around student-specific needs and IEP requirements. It also covers field trips, athletics and special events. Support can extend to driver recruiting, screening and training. Fleet procurement, maintenance and lifecycle planning can sit with the company as well.

Durham has worked with school districts since 1917. It began as a three-bus operation in California's San Gabriel Valley, with early expertise in transporting students with specialized needs. Local operating teams are backed by the broader Summit School Services network for safety, recruiting, maintenance and technology.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "© Copyright 2026 Concur Technologies, Inc. All rights reserved." Fetched https://www.concur.com (curl with browser UA, HTTP 200, 170KB; WebFetch got 403 so I used curl). Page title: "Spend Management Software for Travel, Expense, Invoice | SAP Concur", canonical https://www.concur.com/. Rule 3 check PASSED: this is NOT sap.com. It is the brand's own domain, copyright held by Concur Technologies, Inc., with its own product navigation (Concur Expense, Concur Travel, Concur Invoice, Concur Request, Concur TripLink) and its own solutions nav including "Government", "Government contracting" and "State & local governments". Matches the description (travel, expense and invoice software). CAVEAT the board operator should know: https://www.concur.com/careers 302s off-domain to https://jobs.sap.com/search (unfiltered, all-SAP job search). So the URL is correct as the company's identity page, but any scraper that follows the careers link will inherit SAP's entire global req list rather than SAP Concur roles. Recommend the record carry the site but not auto-scrape jobs.sap.com/search unfiltered.

paragraphs: SAP Concur sells software for handling business expenses, travel and supplier invoices. The pitch is a single platform that gives a company better visibility and control over spending. The company says the products are designed for businesses of all sizes.

Concur Expense is cloud-based expense management software covering the stretch from submitting a receipt to being reimbursed. Key details are pulled from receipts and card transactions automatically, so staff key in less data by hand. Submitted expenses are checked against company rules before they move any further along. A companion product handles the step before money is spent, automating requests and approvals against travel and expense policy. A separate audit product applies machine learning to fraud and compliance risks both before and after reimbursement.

The platform is meant to sit on top of systems a customer already runs, with hundreds of pre-built connectors and open APIs for anything custom. The company says its models are trained on one of the largest expense datasets in the industry and improve as more transactions pass through. Expense pricing is published in US dollars and varies with monthly commitment. The top tier is set aside for businesses that need the most advanced capabilities.

paragraphs: Sparkrock builds the software that powers mission-driven organizations, naming nonprofits, human services, public sector, and K-12 schools as the groups it serves. The operational areas the software covers include finance, procurement, HR management, and payroll. Sparkrock Finance covers approvals, fund visibility, grant management, and automated workflows.

Sparkrock Ed provides ERP, SIS, and school-generated funds management tools to educators. Sparkrock SIS offers student record, attendance, and achievement management in a cloud environment. The SchoolDay platform handles forms, digital permission slips, activities management, and online payments for educators. Sparkrock Impact ERP is aimed at not-for-profit organizations, and tribal governments are named as users of the same product.

Sparkrock Finance and Sparkrock Impact HRP are built on the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central platform. Sparkrock Finance users have built-in Microsoft Copilot AI for analytics, predictive modeling, and forecasting of budgets and cash flow. The company states that it helps schools and nonprofits manage over 100,000 employees and $15 billion in finances every year.

before.name: Bentek
before.description: Benefits administration and enrollment built exclusively for public-sector employers - exhibited at SALGBA 2026

paragraphs: Bentek sells benefits administration software purpose-built for the public sector. The company describes it as designed exclusively for states, local governments and educational institutions. It says its focus is the benefits administration needs of schools, counties and city governments.

The platform is put to work through configurable workflows, automated processes and adaptable reporting tools. It integrates with HRIS and payroll systems so data moves between platforms with less manual entry. Bentek says the platform carries more than 5,000 business rules. A library of more than 60 ready-made reports covers enrollment, engagement and compliance. Self-service enrollment handles active employees, retirees and COBRA participants.

Bentek says it was founded to serve public sector organizations. The company says its story began in 2006. It started when a local school district struggled to manage its benefits. The company puts its experience in the public sector environment at more than 20 years. It says it serves more than 300 employers in the public sector. One story on the site describes helping the Government of the U.S. Virgin Islands transform its benefits administration in four months.

before.name: Red Rover
before.description: Absence, substitute placement and time tracking for school districts

paragraphs: Red Rover builds human resources software for K-12 school districts. The core of it is absence management, substitute scheduling and time tracking. Districts can also run professional development through it, with tracking, approvals and compliance in one place.

When a teacher is out, the system looks for a substitute on its own instead of leaving an office to make calls. Time tracking is meant to sit alongside the system a district already uses. For connecting to other district software, the company says it assigns a technician to each customer until the job is finished.

The founders spent years building and selling substitute placement software for schools before starting this company. They began the current effort in 2020. Red Rover counts more than 2,000 school districts across 49 states. Its homepage puts the number of schools that have switched above 28,000. Published case studies include one on Lake County Schools.

before.name: PaymentWorks
before.description: Supplier onboarding and payee identity verification preventing payments fraud for gov and higher-ed - exhibited at GFOA 2026

paragraphs: PaymentWorks sells software that organizations use to create and maintain vendor records inside their ERP. The company describes the platform as a front door to the ERP that combines vendor onboarding and maintenance, ACH risk transfer, and check-to-digital payment conversion. It is sold into healthcare, higher education, K-12, state and local government, and enterprise.

Each vendor is vetted through what the company calls a proprietary onboarding system before a payment is approved. That onboarding sits on top of a payee network the site puts at more than 1.5 million authenticated payees. Compliance work is automated alongside it, covering sanctions checks, continuous monitoring, W9 and 1099 information, and audit trails. The site states that ACH payments made through the platform are indemnified, with additional coverage available.

Published case studies include the University of North Texas. Another describes a county that fell victim to a $2.5M scam after a request to change vendor banking details. The company says it offers a payments security warranty for fraudulent payments. Its about page introduces a leadership team including a co-founder whose patent work in data management led to the founding of the company.

paragraphs: PowerSchool sells software that school districts run from home to classroom to central office, covering the records, communication, and back-office work of running a school system. The company says its software reaches over 60 million students in 90 countries.

The student information side pulls scattered records into one accurate student record, so staff and families are working from the same source. Teaching and learning products sit alongside it, among them a learning management system. For the central office, finance, human resources, and operations are brought into one connected system. PowerSchool states that PowerBuddy won a 2024 GESS Education Award. In districts already using its products, the company says teachers are reclaiming at least 10 hours a week.

before.name: HopSkipDrive
before.description: Vetted small-vehicle student rides supplementing district bus fleets - exhibited at NAPT Summit 2026, NSBA 2026

hiring.note: Regional Account Manager- Future O (Remote USA)

paragraphs: HopSkipDrive arranges rides for students who cannot be served by a traditional school bus route. The company calls itself a technology company that solves complex transportation challenges where there is a heightened need for safety, equity, and care.

Rides come through a marketplace connecting kids, older adults, or anyone needing extra support to highly vetted caregivers on wheels. The homepage says rides are licensed, regulated, and ready in six hours. Ride types span McKinney-Vento, foster care, special needs and IEPs, charter schools, general education, after school, and career and technical education. Districts also use RouteWise AI, which optimizes routes for buses and small vehicles.

Denver Public Schools is described on the site as using RouteWise AI to optimize its multimodal transportation system. Cypress-Fairbanks Independent School District decided to outsource its McKinney-Vento and a portion of foster transportation to the company. Counties, government agencies, and nonprofits are also named as groups the company supports. It traces its start to three working moms trying to get their busy kids to and from school and activities.

before.scope_note: Overwhelmingly a SLED vendor - the homepage customer wall is almost entirely named school districts, and /government-agencies/ names a state HHS department and two county agencies. before.name: CommunityPass
before.description: Online registration, membership, and payments for parks & rec departments and community schools - exhibited at NRPA 2026

paragraphs: CommunityPass is cloud-based software that powers schools, recreation centers, community organizations, and sports leagues. It comes from Capturepoint, whose founder the company names as Joe Oriente.

The product began in 2002 with a town Sports Council overwhelmed by hundreds of paper registration forms as athletic sign-ups climbed. The answer was a single account on one website through which families reach registration for every participating organization in town. Departments can offer registration for classes, activities, programs, and trips, with options to buy merchandise and tickets. Payments accept multiple forms with recurring billing and plans while maintaining PCI compliance.

Check-in and check-out are contactless and digital, with pick-up timestamps and real-time emergency contact information for authorized parents. Staff can choose from 300+ pre-built reports covering attendance, financial, roster, and statistical data, or build their own. The company says CommunityPass has grown to serve parks and recreation organizations and schools all across the country.

before.name: Frontline Education
before.description: K-12 HR, absence and substitute management, and operations software

paragraphs: Frontline Education sells software that school districts use to run hiring, onboarding, payroll, absences, and professional development as connected systems. The pitch is that it joins up the tools teachers, staff, and administrators rely on in one place.

Beyond personnel work, it helps special educators and school nurses manage documentation, compliance, and reporting. Business-side tools help district leaders track key areas so they can understand spending and oversee district resources. Published case studies describe districts modernizing hiring on connected recruiting workflows.

The company says its software supports over 4.1 million users daily in education across the US and abroad. District data is monitored around the clock in five physically and geographically secure datacenters in the United States and Canada. The security page states SOC 2 certification and Texas RAMP certification for selling software solutions in Texas. It also says its products and security program are aligned with FERPA and HIPAA. The company signed the Student Privacy Pledge.

before.name: Highland Electric Fleets
before.description: Electric school bus fleet-as-a-service subscriptions for districts - exhibited at NSBA 2026

paragraphs: Highland Electric Fleets sells fleet electrification as a service to school districts, municipalities and fleet operators. The company was founded in 2019.

Customers hand over the whole job, and Highland plans, procures, implements and optimizes the electric fleet on their behalf. A performance guarantee reimburses customers for down time if the fleet is not charged and route-ready. The commercial pitch is that an electric fleet can be operated at or below the cost of running a diesel one. Highland also secures grants and incentives on behalf of the agencies it works with.

The company serves as the Official Electric School Bus Provider of the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games and Team USA. It points to vehicle-to-grid work and to managing some of the largest electric school bus fleets in the country. Maintenance figures cited on the site come from Twin Rivers Unified School District, which operates 58 EV buses. The site also counts the states where it has operational and contracted projects.

before.name: First Student
before.description: Contracted school bus transportation services for K-12 districts - exhibited at NAPT Summit 2026

paragraphs: First Student moves students to and from school, with a stated mission of the safest, most reliable and most efficient ride. School districts are its partners, in communities big and small.

The company reports more than 48,000 vehicles, including electric buses. It lists over 530 locations across two countries. By its own count, those buses carry 4.8 million student journeys a day. A technology platform called HALO oversees the transportation journey. One piece of it, First View, is a vehicle tracker app for parents and caregivers. Buses can also be rented for events and field trips through a charter quote.

The company says it has provided a safe and reliable experience for nearly half a century. In one award citation it was recognized in a transportation category for HALO's safety tools, predictive maintenance and real-time visibility. A mascot named Safety Dog teaches students about safe school bus behavior. The mascot travels a coast-to-coast, back-to-school tour. Its leadership team spans transportation management, technology and electrification.

before.name: KNOWiNK
before.description: Poll Pad electronic poll books - the market leader - plus election-day management tools

paragraphs: KNOWiNK sells the Poll Pad electronic poll book system, which handles voter check-in and verification at the polls. Poll Pad is offered as a replacement for paper poll books, which the page calls a cause of long lines at the polls and of inefficient election record keeping. Poll Pad includes ePulse, a centralized election management interface supporting real-time data transfer and audit capabilities.

The wider product suite adds a paper ballot printing system built to give election officials the right quantity of ballots for every election. A voter registration and election management system covers the accuracy and integrity of election information. The pages name jurisdictions and election officials as the users, and say the software reduces preparation time and simplifies election administration.
KNOWiNK is based in St. Louis and was founded by Scott Leiendecker. The company describes itself as family-owned and reports more than 150 employees.

quote.text: Fast and secure voter verification to replace the outdated and inefficient paper poll books that are often the cause of long lines at the polls and inefficient election record keeping.

provenance.quote: This electronic poll book streamlines voter check-in and verification, enhancing election efficiency and security.
Fast and secure voter verification to replace the outdated and inefficient paper poll books that are often the cause of long lines at the polls and inefficient election record keeping.
Featuring ePulse, a centralized election management interface, Poll Pad® enables real-time data transfer, audit capabilities, and improved voter history accuracy.
A secure, high-quality paper ballot printing system developed to ensure ballot accuracy by providing election officials the right quantity of ballots for every election.
Secure voter registration and election management system to ensure accuracy and integrity of all election information.
Designed for ease of use, it helps jurisdictions enhance transparency, reduce preparation time, and simplify election administration.
Based in St. Louis, KNOWiNK was founded by Scott Leiendecker, a nationally respected election expert.
KNOWiNK is a family-owned election security and technology company built exclusively in America and now has more than 150 employees.

before.name: Clariti
before.description: Community development permitting and licensing software (founded as BasicGov) - exhibited at ICC 2026

paragraphs: Clariti sells community development software to local governments, pitched at any size and budget. One edition is permitting software for large local governments. A second, Launch, is aimed at small to mid-sized local governments. A third product, CivCheck, uses AI to guide applicants toward a complete and compliant submission and staff through every check.

The software keeps the permit counter online, where applicants apply, pay, and track status. It also tracks code violations from report to resolution, with automatic case assignment and links to local zoning and codes. Staff can build a report, adjust a page layout, or create a new permit type themselves. The large-jurisdiction edition runs on the Salesforce Platform, whose APIs let a government connect its other tools. Launch customers can copy a peer's permitting workflows using a cloning tool. On the AI side, staff have to approve every interpretation the software makes.

The company says the large-jurisdiction product was built with input from government customers over 16 years. Its home page names Los Angeles, Phoenix, and Orange County among the cities and counties using Clariti. Launch pricing is stated as based on population rather than user count.

before.name: OpenAI
before.description: ChatGPT and the API, sold to public sector including named state and local government roles

paragraphs: OpenAI describes itself as an AI research and deployment company. Its stated mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. Alongside the research, it sells its models to organizations.

The solutions pages sort the offer by the work it is meant to do, and one of the listed uses is supporting essential public services. Another is education, aimed at students, educators, and researchers. Customers can connect their own data to ChatGPT through custom MCP servers. For buyers who need controls, the company points to encryption and configurable policies for keeping data private.

Recent release notes lean toward regulated and enterprise buyers: mutual TLS and X.509 workload identity federation are generally available for the API. Healthcare plugins are available to eligible ChatGPT for Healthcare and HIPAA-enabled ChatGPT Enterprise workspaces. The company says it consists of a nonprofit foundation and a for-profit group, with the foundation governing the group.

quote.text: We are building safe and beneficial AGI, but will also consider our mission fulfilled if our work aids others to achieve this outcome.

before.name: Forerunner
before.description: Floodplain management software: NFIP/CRS compliance, elevation certificates; $26.3M Series B - exhibited at StormCon 2026, ICC 2026

paragraphs: Forerunner sells software it calls a geospatial intelligence layer. The platform unifies geospatial data, field operations, and AI-powered workflows in one place. Local government is a core buyer, with compliance work across stormwater, floodplain, and code enforcement programs. The company also markets to energy and infrastructure operators handling inspections across active sites and assets.

At the base sits a map-first view holding every asset, permit parcel, violation, and environmental layer. On top of it run configurable workflows for inspections, permits, violations, and grant tracking. Inspection findings then generate corrective actions, and permit deadlines trigger notifications. The company says adoption brings no rip-and-replace projects and no major workflow disruptions. It claims teams are up and running in weeks.

Published case studies name the Puerto Rico Planning Board, which the company says replaced paper forms and spreadsheets for field inspections and code compliance. Another states that Lee County saves approximately 16 hours of staff time per week. A further case study describes Ponce Inlet centralizing National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System workflows to reclaim 10 or more hours per week.

brands.name: Simpleview (Granicus Destinations)
brands.description:
Simpleview sells destination-marketing technology and marketing services to the organizations that promote places. Its own homepage now carries the title "Granicus Destinations | Marketing Solutions | CVB Tourism Software" and the line "From small towns to big countries, Granicus Destinations is the tourism software partner to help you engage stakeholders, attract visitors, and win bids for conventions and events." The product menu lists Simpleview CMS, "designed by and for DMOs"; Simpleview CRM, an industry-specific CRM with "seamless integration with more than 20 programs"; Simpleview DAM for digital assets; Destination Canvas; an Online Booking & Referral Engine branded Book > Direct that "lets visitors book directly with your partners and stakeholders"; Partner Engagement & Website Monetization (DTN), which "facilitates targeted advertising on destination websites" so DMOs can earn revenue; user-generated content; mobile apps; digital accessibility; email marketing and automation via Act-On; digital proposals; event management; short-term rental solutions; and a data tier of Simpleview Data Engine, dashboards, pace reporting and a meetings and groups database. Alongside the software it sells agency work: website design, visual identity, SEO, paid media, digital strategy, a Digital Maturity Model, DMO partner engagement, the Digital Influence Report and training. The acquisition release describes the buyers as "convention bureaus, venues, tourism boards, destination marketing organizations, and attractions." Granicus's destinations page states that "more than 500 DMOs use our CMS," that "1,000-plus destinations" use the CRM, and that 400M+ people visit those websites annually.

Both sites confirm Simpleview is part of Granicus, so the careers redirect is corroborated rather than relied on. Granicus's destinations FAQ asks "Is Simpleview now part of Granicus?" and answers "Yes. Simpleview was acquired by Granicus, and the legacy Simpleview products, services, expertise, and thought leadership are now a part of the Granicus portfolio serving destination marketers," then explains the two-site split: the solutions "remain at simpleviewinc.com" during a transition and "The two websites will be combined in the near future." Granicus's own office list gives Tucson, AZ, 8950 N. Oracle Road as "Simpleview, now part of Granicus" - the address in Simpleview's footer. Simpleview's Our Story page says plainly "We were acquired by Granicus." The Granicus press release of September 5, 2024 announced the acquisition, said Simpleview "works with more than 1,000 premier destinations," quoted Simpleview CEO Ryan George, and put the combined company at more than 7,000 organizations and roughly 2,000 employees. A May 5, 2026 release then announced Granicus Destinations as "a dedicated business segment" with its own leadership and the DXC platform, "supporting more than 1,000 destinations worldwide, including all 11 FIFA World Cup host cities." Our Story dates the business to 2001 as 220 Solutions, founded by Ryan George, Bill Simpson and Scott Wood; the first web-based CRM built for DMOs in 2002, with Visit Lauderdale as first client; a 2007 merger with cvbTV at 100 clients; New Media Gateway in 2010; Software Management, Inc. in 2014, adding 92 DMOs; and later 2Synergize, Jackrabbit Systems, Eventsforce and the MINT+ meetings database.

profile_research.description:
Granicus sells cloud software and services that governments use to communicate with the public, publish and stream meetings, run websites and forms, and manage records and permits. Its own site frames the offering as two platforms: the Government Experience Cloud (GXC), split into Service Cloud ("Deliver services without friction"), Engagement Cloud ("Grow and activate audiences") and Operations Cloud ("Automate workflows and reduce costs"), and the Destination Experience Cloud (DXC) for destination marketing. Layered on those are Government Experience Agent (GXA), described as an AI-powered digital agent built for government, a Federal Experience Cloud, and the GXI Enterprise and GXI Foundations intelligence tiers. The solution pages group the underlying products into agenda and meeting management, websites and CMS, digital services and forms, digital communication and engagement, permitting and licensing, and public records and short-term-rental compliance. The product directory names each tool with its legacy brand in parentheses: Communications (govDelivery), Websites & CMS (govAccess, OpenCities, Intranet), Records Request Management (GovQA and GovQA Legal), Short-Term Rentals (Host Compliance), Forms & Workflow (OpenForms), Service Request Management (govService and OneView), Permitting, Compliance & Licensing (AMANDA and SmartGov), Land & Official Records (govRecords), Sentiment & Feedback (EngagementHQ), Video (self-managed, and Swagit partially and fully managed), Boards and Commissions, and agenda management under the Legistar, OneMeeting and Peak names. The buyers named under "Who we serve" are local government, state government, federal government, education, special districts, elected officials and destinations, with country sites for Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia & New Zealand, India, and Latin America & the Caribbean. Granicus also sells consulting and digital agency work through the Granicus Experience Group (GXG).

Granicus is the parent of this family rather than a member of one. Its company page states "more than 2,000 employees across the globe supporting more than 7,000 public sector organizations," and the careers page repeats "about 2,000 of us" spread across "eight countries" in a remote-first workplace; that page's "Explore roles" button points at careers-granicus.icims.com, the iCIMS board the Simpleview careers page also lands on. The homepage figure block claims 7,000+ public sector customers, 360M people in the Granicus subscriber network, 100% of U.S. federal cabinet-level agencies, 48 of the 50 largest U.S. cities, 30B digital experiences and 22B government messages delivered annually, 8B government website views, 3.5M online forms submitted, 2M record requests served and 123K government meetings streamed each year. The company page carries a timeline headed "Organic and inorganic growth through best-in-class acquisitions": Granicus and GovDelivery were independently founded in 1999 and merged in 2017; Vision Internet arrived in 2018; a London-based government service provider in 2019; Bang the Table, OpenCities and GovQA in 2021 alongside Australia/New Zealand expansion; a full-service video provider and a government CRM in 2022 with entry into Latin America and the Caribbean; Simpleview in 2024; and GXA's launch in 2025. The same page names Vista Equity Partners as an existing investor joined by Harvest Partners in 2020. The trust-center office list gives Denver, Washington DC, Tucson, Ottawa, London, Melbourne, Auckland, San Juan and Bengaluru.

paragraphs: Partake sells a sharing platform built around an app that lets people borrow and lend household goods within a local area. The company describes the product as a turnkey solution that gives members access to what their community already owns. Onboarding is described as creating a profile for free and finding a local hub, with searching, requesting and returning items as the steps that follow.

The homepage sets out four paths: citizen, cities and municipalities, business and organization, and building a platform of your own. For cities and municipalities, the offer is a fully supported, turnkey sharing solution aimed at letting citizens share, save and connect. A parallel offer for business and organizations covers employees and members on the same supported, turnkey basis.

A separate platform offer lets an organization deploy a sharing ecosystem tailored to its industry, with the infrastructure, safety framework and expertise supplied by the company. The stated mission is to make sharing the obvious choice so that every community can unlock its collective abundance. The frequently asked questions page lists question headings, including what happens if an item is damaged or broken.

paragraphs: Hello Heart sells a heart health program that combines connected devices, clinical expertise and AI-based guidance. Employers, health plans and labor unions are named as the organizations that work with the company to reach their people.

Members take daily readings with an FDA-cleared monitor. The app keeps blood pressure, cholesterol, weight, activity and medications in one place. A separate medication service brings together an AI assistant, a connected pill box and pharmacist-led reviews. That assistant is available at any hour for common heart health questions.

The company describes itself as an AI company focused on preventive heart health. It lists offices in the United States and Israel. It also says it is part of the American Heart Association Innovators network. Public employers appear among its client stories, including the City of Minneapolis, Minnesota, where cardiovascular conditions are called a top three cost driver.

before.name: Placemetry
before.description: AI street-imagery analysis: pavement condition, sign inventory, and blight for public works and code enforcement

paragraphs: Placemetry drives a city and captures photos from the public right-of-way, then analyzes properties and roadways with AI so departments can get ahead of problems rather than react to them. Each vehicle is equipped with three high-resolution cameras, one facing forward and one facing to each side, capturing street-level imagery in a single drive. Forward-facing cameras deliver per-segment pavement condition, an asset inventory, and safety screening in a single pass.

Side cameras capture a wide view of the public right-of-way in one pass, including properties, yards, sidewalks, trees, and vegetation. The same dataset feeds Code Enforcement, Economic Development, and Forestry & Parks. All imagery is captured from the public right-of-way, faces and license plates are blurred, and the city owns the data.

One cadence is a single citywide survey with no subscription required. Another is a quarterly or bi-annual citywide sweep in which Placemetry teams drive every street and the AI scores properties. A third option puts cameras on city vehicles the city already operates, so garbage trucks and street sweepers capture passive citywide coverage. Delivery runs through direct API integrations, standard spreadsheet downloads, or a secure web app, with REST API Endpoints and Webhooks.

quote.text: If you can see it from the street, we can measure it.

Best for roadway and housing inventory. A single citywide survey. The fastest way to see what’s on the street. We make it easy: no subscription required.
Best for tracking program impact. Quarterly or bi-annual citywide sweeps. Our teams drive every street and our AI scores properties. You get the insights; we handle the mileage.

Best for supporting code compliance. Our cameras on city vehicles you already operate. Garbage trucks and street sweepers capture passive citywide coverage; code & parking enforcement vehicles cover priority areas on demand.

Access our platform via direct API integrations, standard spreadsheet downloads, or our secure web app to power every city department. Deploy via clean REST API Endpoints and Webhooks with zero local installation.

before.name: ES&S (Election Systems & Software)
before.description: The largest US voting systems vendor: tabulators, ballot marking, election management (founded as AIS)

paragraphs: ES&S has supplied election systems since 1979, describing them as secure, accessible and accurate. By its own account the systems are paper based, certified and fully auditable. They are sold to jurisdictions large and small.

The catalog includes ballot marking devices and tabulators. The DS950 handles Election Day, absentee and early vote ballots. On the ExpressVote, voters insert a card to activate the voting session, and the ballot is then dispensed for voter review. That device supports any language in audio and more than 30 languages in text. The ExpressVote XL displays the full ballot on a 32-inch interactive screen and produces an independent voter-verifiable paper record. Paired with an electronic pollbook, a polling place can check in voters and serve up to 15,000 different ballot styles. The ExpressVote 3 uses Secure Boot and application allowlisting to verify that only the certified operating system, software and firmware are on the unit.

ES&S says it has 31 voting systems certified by the U.S. Election Assistance Commission. It describes partnering with the Department of Homeland Security on industry practices. The company presents itself as part of the American Council for Election Technology. Its latest average rating by customers on overall satisfaction is given as 4.63 out of 5.

before.name: COLBI Technologies
before.description: Capital program management and purchasing/AP compliance for 140+ California districts

paragraphs: COLBI Technologies develops software tools that help public agencies manage their capital building programs. It also provides in-person, hands-on training and support through a team of fiscal, construction, and facility experts.

Account-Ability, its program management application, rests on what the company calls three critical components. COLBIDocs puts agencies in control of their documents and processes without paying for expensive IT and storage systems. QualityBidders is a web-based tool that simplifies the prequalification process for contractors and agencies. It gives contractors an efficient way to comply with prequalification and CUPCCAA requirements. SecureBids provides an online, secure place to receive bids electronically.

The company maintains a national presence serving school districts and public agencies. It says it serves more than 250 clients managing more than 45 billion in capital building program dollars. It points to large capital building programs over the past 20 years in both California and Texas. The company came together after Lettie Boggs reached out to Chuck Olsen, an entrepreneur in computer programming, and it started in his garage.

before.name: Avila
before.description: AI grants platform: finds eligible grants, drafts applications, manages compliance

paragraphs: Avila sells an AI grant platform aimed at local government. The site says it finds the opportunities an agency qualifies for and writes its proposals. It also says it helps governments, schools and nonprofits discover and apply for funding.

Discovery matches state, local, regional and foundation opportunities to a customer's own projects. For applications, the platform simplifies dense notices of funding opportunity into clearer requirements. It fills in federal forms including SF-424, SF-424A, SF-LLL and program-specific attachments. Once an award lands, it ingests invoices and auto-categorizes expenses against the approved budget. It also flags compliance issues against 2 CFR 200 and the awarding agency's rules.

Users named on the site include the Houston-Galveston Area Council. One case study describes a mid-sized county government in the western U.S. Another describes a statewide public university system in the northeast. The company states that it is SOC 2 compliant. It says all data is encrypted in transit and at rest. The about page says NVIDIA Inception, Microsoft for Startups and MongoDB have welcomed the company into their programs.

paragraphs: Intrado sells call handling and management systems for emergency response. It describes itself as the connective tissue that gets the right help to the right location as quickly as possible.

Alongside the call center products, one line keeps employees safe wherever they work while meeting state and federal regulations. Another covers incident management for schools from prevention through response and recovery. For carriers, call routing, location and data products connect subscribers to emergency services and keep providers compliant. Network services are offered to improve call routing and data sharing and to deliver on i3 compliance. ECaTS, the Emergency Call Tracking System, generates descriptive reports from 9-1-1 call data.

The company puts its history in the emergency services industry at 45 years. That history includes acquisitions of Lucent Public Safety, Positron Public Safety Systems, ECaTS, 911 ETC and 911 Enable. Headquarters are in Longmont, Colorado, with a manufacturing site in Montreal, Quebec. The company reports approximately 950 employees worldwide, most of them in the Longmont and Montreal regions.

paragraphs: ZOLL makes medical devices, software and related services for patients with serious cardiopulmonary and respiratory conditions. Its buyers include hospitals and other healthcare organizations, emergency medical services and militaries.

One part of the catalog covers acute cardiac care, from sudden cardiac death protection to heart failure management and care after a heart attack. Another covers diagnostics meant to widen access to sleep apnea testing. There is also ventilation technology for patients from neonates to adults. The Zenix monitor/defibrillator is offered for EMS and hospital use. The history page records the launch of RescueNet, described as an EMS information management system covering patient care, operational efficiency and agency compliance. A subsidiary was later renamed ZOLL Data Systems to better reflect the EMS market.

The company traces its origins to Dr. Paul Zoll, a physician who co-founded it in 1980. The history page lists the co-founders as Dr. Zoll, Leigh Stein and Thomas Claflin. Its policy for interactions with health care professionals is based on the Advanced Medical Technology Association Code of Ethics. The company also certifies a compliance program satisfying the requirements of the California Health and Safety Code. Under the Sunshine Act it tracks payments and other transfers of value and reports them annually.

paragraphs: Quester Tangent manufactures, supplies, and integrates passenger train technologies for new train build projects and for midlife renewal of existing fleets. The product line pairs Trainwise, an onboard train control and monitoring system (TCMS) and passenger information system (PIS), with Fleetwise, a wayside enterprise fleet management system (EFMS).

Train manufacturers fast-track production using integrated Trainwise TCMS and PIS technology tailored to the needs of each project. Transit authorities and operators use Fleetwise EFMS to connect from the wayside to the onboard Trainwise TCMS and PIS of every train in a fleet. The fleets named are subway, LRV, and commuter rail, and the systems serve drivers, operations, maintenance, and engineering teams.

Operations teams determine fleet readiness and see train faults in real-time, while maintenance teams triage service affecting repairs and automate system software updates. Quester Tangent states more than two decades of passenger train experience and thousands of units in revenue service with major transit authorities. Delivery covers hardware and software design, manufacturing, project management, and turnkey delivery with integration and in-house engineering services for all types of train networks.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "© AT&T Intellectual Property. All rights reserved. FirstNet and the FirstNet logo are registered trademarks and service marks of the First Responder Network Authority." Fetched https://www.firstnet.com. The entity question in the CAUTION resolves cleanly: the footer copyright is AT&T's ('© AT&T Intellectual Property'), while the FirstNet marks are acknowledged as belonging to the First Responder Network Authority — i.e. this domain is the AT&T-operated commercial service, which is exactly the board entity 'FirstNet, Built with AT&T'. I confirmed the split by also fetching the federal side: firstnetauthority.gov states 'The First Responder Network Authority is an independent agency within the U.S. Department of Commerce's National Telecommunications and Information Administration' and sends users elsewhere for service with 'Access my FirstNet account (FirstNet.com).' So .gov is the agency, .com is the AT&T service. On rule 3: firstnet.com is NOT the parent's corporate domain (that is att.com) — it is the product's own dedicated domain with its own branding, plans and support, so it is acceptable. FLAG for the board operator, though: FirstNet does not recruit as a separate employer. Sales roles on this product are posted as AT&T requisitions, so a scraper pointed at firstnet.com will like

paragraphs: The company sells election technology, and states its aim as delivering systems that are transparent, secure, accessible and reliable. Its site says the business was formed through the acquisition of Dominion Voting Systems and now trades as Liberty Vote. It describes itself as an American-owned nonpartisan election technology company.

The product range covers the election from ballot design through vote capture to results reporting. An election management system runs the whole election project from one database. Ballot marking devices come in configurations for in-person, accessible and early voting. Central count scanners handle absentee, vote-by-mail and precinct ballots. An audit record lets officials review ballot images alongside how the tabulator read each ballot. The systems work with verifiable paper ballots.

Customers are the jurisdictions it serves, and the company says older systems were retired so each one runs supported technology. In late 2025 it submitted a voting system called Frontier 1.0 to the U.S. Election Assistance Commission for certification under VVSG 2.0 standards. The company is owned by its founder and chairman, Scott Leiendecker.

paragraphs: Netsmart sells healthcare software to community-based care providers, offering an integrated platform of healthcare technology and services meant to simplify workflows. The Netsmart CareFabric platform is presented as the framework of care solutions and services available to those providers. CareRecord solutions are tailored EHRs for human services, post-acute, physical therapy and geriatric care communities. Care Administration covers revenue cycle management, collection management, payment portals and clearinghouse work.

The pages name human services, post-acute, public sector, physical therapy and PALTC organizations as the communities served. Within human services, the platform scales across behavioral health, addiction treatment, autism, I/DD, child and family services, public health and integrated care. Public Sector EHR software is described as coordinating care across city, state, county and community agencies. The addiction treatment page describes substance use records supporting SAMHSA Opioid Treatment Programs and medication-assisted treatment.

paragraphs: VirTra sells immersive simulation training that prepares law enforcement, military, and public-safety professionals to make better decisions under pressure. before.name: Justice Systems by LONG
before.description: Design-build electronic security integration for jails and courts: surveillance, access, detention controls

paragraphs: LONG DBA Justice Systems is a design-build integrator of unified electronic security systems, specializing in government and public safety facilities. The services offered are design-build integration, competitive-bid integration, and follow-on maintenance, applied to new construction, upgrades, and retrofits. Retrofit and upgrade work covers general government buildings, courts, jails, juvenile facilities, secure mental health facilities, and prisons.

Integration is built on PLCs, described as enabling single-point responsibility for high-security buildings. The unified package covers door and elevator controls, video surveillance, intercommunications, paging, utility controls, and alarm monitoring. Justice Systems serves as engineer-of-record on a large percentage of its projects and holds professional engineering registration in multiple states.

Reported volume is 120 projects and $50 million in total systems value, counting only the contract value of projects performed. Follow-on service and support has covered approximately 70% of the facilities built or upgraded, some $7 million in maintenance services. Procurement can run through NASPO, where LONG is an authorized dealer in Washington, Colorado, and Alaska.

before.name: Geographic Solutions
before.description: Workforce case management and job-matching systems for state workforce agencies - exhibited at NASWA 2025

paragraphs: Geographic Solutions makes online software for agencies in workforce development, economic development, education, corrections, human services, and unemployment insurance. The company frames that work as case management, labor exchange, and service delivery.

Its VOS Sapphire suite handles federally funded partner programs under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act, along with job aggregation, labor market information, fund tracking, federal reporting, and unemployment insurance benefits. The Virtual OneStop line is sold on a SaaS basis under annual or multi-year agreements covering hosting, maintenance, and upgrades. A map on the site lists the client systems built for each state.

Founder and President Paul Toomey started the business in 1992. The company timeline dates the first labor market information system in the country to a 1994 launch in North Carolina. The software suite has achieved StateRAMP/GovRAMP Authorization. Geographic Solutions also states that it is currently SOC1 Type II, SOC2 Type II, and SOC3 certified. Among its listed affiliations is membership in the National Association of Colleges and Employers.

paragraphs: Echodyne designs, manufactures and delivers commercial radar systems built around a technology it calls MESA. Its customers are systems suppliers, integrators and end users in defense, government, critical infrastructure protection, C-UAS and UAS/AAM markets in more than 40 countries. MESA stands for metamaterials electronically scanned array, and the company holds global patents on those radar architectures.

The radars are aimed at counter-UAS and multi-domain missions, where the company says they improve safety and security outcomes. Configurations range from fixed installations to rapid setup portable kits, and Echodyne describes MIL-STD reliability at COTS availability. The company has announced an Android Team Awareness Kit plugin that lets users configure, control and visualize data from its radars within ATAK.
Radars are manufactured outside Seattle, Washington, in the United States. Echodyne is AS9100 and ISO 9001 certified. AS9100 is a standardized quality management system for the aerospace industry.
