paragraphs: Penlink sells a digital intelligence platform to public safety agencies and enterprises, which use it to turn complex data into intelligence for investigations and security work. The platform brings together digital evidence, open-source intelligence, data analytics and live communications to support complex investigations. The company says it has worked alongside law enforcement, national security and corporate safety professionals for nearly forty years.

Its evidence product, PLX, ingests and normalizes call detail records, tower dumps, social media warrants, email returns, tracking data and mobile extractions into one dashboard. Through PLX the platform also supports lawful live collection of phone calls, texts and web activity. For open-source work, Tangles automates the search and analysis of data from the open, deep and dark web. An AI layer the company calls CoAnalyst360 orchestrates workflows and maintains context from first query to final outcome across open-source intelligence, evidence and live communications. It coordinates discovery, analysis and follow-up across PLX, Tangles and GeoTime in a single workflow.

The homepage states that more than 1,000 agencies use Penlink. It lists SOC 2, ISO and CJIS compliance. The company reports that one agency raised its solvability rate from 28% to over 40% in its first month using PLX. A partnership with Chainalysis brings blockchain intelligence into the platform, connecting on-chain activity to identities, communications and locations.

paragraphs: Skydio makes autonomous drones, along with the docks and software to run them, and sells drone programs to customers from energy networks to neighborhood precincts to battlefields. Those programs cover Drone as First Responder, automated inspection and site security. Dock for X10 positions Skydio X10 drones at a site so that missions launch remotely without anyone present. The smaller Skydio R10 puts eyes indoors before officers enter.

Skydio states that more than 1,500 public safety agencies use its drones. In a Drone as First Responder program, Skydio says its drones launch in under 20 seconds and reach incidents autonomously in under 90 seconds. DFR Command is the software from which remote operators launch and manage drones, respond to multiple calls and stream live video to patrol and command. It integrates with RapidSOS and CAD at dispatch, Axon Fusus for live operations, and automatic evidence upload into Axon Evidence. Skydio's customer stories include Brookhaven PD, which it says reached 30 second response times after deploying 8 Docks.

Skydio Site Security uses the same dock-based drones to verify alarms, patrol perimeters and deliver live visibility across a site. Video streams into Genetec or Milestone, and flights launch automatically when triggered by alarms or access control events. Skydio says its data is encrypted in transit and at rest and that it aligns to SOC 2, ISO 27001 and NIST frameworks.

before.name: DigitalOptometrics
before.description: Tele-optometry platform for remote comprehensive eye exams with a dedicated corrections vertical

paragraphs: DigitalOptometrics is a technology company whose software lets a patient sitting in an optical exam location receive a comprehensive eye examination from a licensed optometrist working somewhere else. The exam and the prescription are meant to be done in under 30 minutes.

The visit starts with preliminary testing carried out on site in the clinical area. A video slit lamp records high-definition footage of the outside structures of the eye for the remote doctor to evaluate. That doctor can control the phoropter remotely and reviews the findings in real time. A comprehensive exam is described as covering ten subject areas, including a vision analysis. At the end the optometrist finalizes and delivers the glasses or contact lens prescription within minutes.

Buyers are optical providers, and the company describes itself as optometrist founded and optometrist driven. Dr. Fried formed the company in 2016 and assembled a team of optical software development specialists. The technology was shown publicly at the Vision Expo in New York City. The company states that its system is used in more than 30 states in the United States and in Canada.

before.name: 4Sight Labs
before.description: OverWatch continuous biometric wearables monitoring detainee vitals for overdose and suicide early warning - exhibited at Michigan Sheriffs Association 2026

paragraphs: 4Sight Labs sells a biometric monitoring system for correctional facilities, meant to help staff watch over the health of people held in custody. Its main product, OverWatch, is presented as the core of a unified correctional biometric platform built for settings where ordinary monitoring falls short.

People in custody wear sensors that track heart rate, blood oxygen, skin temperature and motion, along with other indicators of physiological distress. Readings are processed as they arrive, so that anomalies produce structured notifications instead of an after-the-fact review. Thresholds can be set by the facility so staff hear about a pattern that points toward a crisis.

The company says the platform is built for county detention centers, state systems, private facilities and complex housing units. It also states that the technology is designed and manufactured in the United States, with a controlled hardware and firmware supply chain. The site reports that the Harford County Sheriff's Office publicly announced putting OverWatch into its custody and safety strategy.

quote.text: Continuous biometric monitoring allows staff to identify physiological deterioration before it escalates into an emergency.

before.name: Liberty Defense
before.description: HEXWAVE walk-through concealed weapons detection plus body and shoe scanners for aviation checkpoints and public venues.

paragraphs: Liberty Defense makes AI-based detection equipment for finding concealed weapons and other threats in urban security and aviation settings. Its main product, HEXWAVE, is a walkthrough portal that screens for nonmetallic and metallic threats without asking people to remove shoes, jewelry, belts or jackets.

It uses active millimeter wave, video-rate 3D imaging and AI to detect concealed metallic and non-metallic weapons and other prohibited items. The company says the imaging captures over 400,000 voxels. No images are stored, and none are accessible by the security operator. The operator sees only a go or no-go screen with a clear alert. For aviation, Liberty holds exclusive licenses to two solutions developed by PNNL and funded by the Department of Homeland Security.

The home page states that Liberty delivers HEXWAVE to the TSA. It also says the company is developing screening for aviation workers. Named settings include hotels, schools, airports, public transit systems, places of religion and entertainment venues. On its finances, the company reports completing an initial public offering in the United States that raised approximately $20 million in gross proceeds.

before.name: Black Creek Integrated Systems
before.description: Detention security electronics, jail management software, and inmate RFID tracking for county jails

paragraphs: Black Creek Integrated Systems provides integrated security systems for prisons, jails and detention facilities. It also sells records management software for law enforcement. The company says it was founded in 1978 and has served correctional and public safety agencies nationwide and abroad. It says it was the first to bring touchscreen technology to corrections, in 1989.

Its touchscreen system brings door control, CCTV, intercoms and paging, access control, and utility monitoring together as one console. The design is open architecture, using commercially available components. A licensed mobile device provides physical security management such as locking control and intercom call-ins. Facilities can install NFC tags for officers to scan while walking watch tours. A wellbeing application monitors detainees in detox, with chronic conditions, or on suicide watch. It uses wrist-worn sensors that track heart rate, skin temperature and blood oxygen saturation and detect tampering.

The jail management platform is browser-based and built for county and local jails, handling inmate records, biometrics and analytical reporting. Those jails, the company writes, face a concentration of acute risks including early-phase medical crises, suicide and violence. Record keeping is described as CJIS-compliant data collection and record management.

paragraphs: Flash AI builds investigative software in Ohio for law enforcement agencies. Its main product, Flash PD, takes an entire caseload of video, audio, images, documents and phone extractions into one unified system. Flash PD accepts 115+ file types and processes them in parallel. Investigators then ask questions in plain language and get direct answers with linked source evidence and timestamps.

A second product, Flash Signal, connects to a correctional facility's call recording system so recorded inmate calls flow in as they happen, or historical libraries can be uploaded in batch. Each call is transcribed and scored low, medium or high risk from its content, language and behavioral signals, so investigators open the high-risk calls first. The company says a 60-day pilot at a correctional facility identified 33,004 high-risk signals with zero manual review hours required.

A third product, Flash Chat, extends private AI chat and document analysis to the rest of an agency, with a free trial for the standard deployment and CJIS deployments available by demo. Flash AI states that queries, uploads and conversations are never used to train AI models, and that hosting is on AWS infrastructure in the United States. The customers page lists Whitehall Police Department and Perry Township Police Department as active deployments, and Muskingum County and Guernsey County sheriff's offices as previous pilots.

before.source: NSA 2026; Michigan Sheriffs Association 2026; North Carolina Sheriffs' Association 2026

paragraphs: GUARDIAN RFID sells jails a way to track inmates, run guard tours and log activity as it happens. Fixed readers identify inmates by RFID wristband or RFID card to confirm presence and location. The company is the exclusive distributor of the Clincher wristbands those readers use.

Behind the hardware sits Command Cloud, a platform of integrated applications and services for corrections staff. Long-range readers create customizable zones over housing units, out of cell areas and corridors. Officers carry a rugged Android handheld for data collection and evidence gathering. Check frequencies can be configured by location and inmate classification. Electronic medication orders carry administration times, allergies, dosage, frequencies and routes.

The company says over 75,000 corrections staff across the United States rely on it. Facilities need no servers of their own, since the system is cloud based. It integrates with a wide range of jail management systems as well as offender and case management systems. An ongoing System Renewal Fee covers software upgrades for Command Cloud and Mobile Command. That fee is invoiced 12 months after go-live.

before.name: OD Security North America
before.description: SOTER RS low-dose transmission X-ray body scanners for jails and state prisons

paragraphs: OD Security North America, a Women-Owned Small Business, is the North American distributor of the SOTER RS Full Body Security Scanning System and a strategic R&D partner to OD Security BV. The company was established in late 2012, is based out of College Station, Texas, and grew its team from the Healthcare and Medical X-Ray industry. The company describes the SOTER RS as a contact-free search procedure with no safety risk to Staff.

Contraband detection for Law Enforcement, Corrections and Community Justice Agencies is the stated market, and the company says the challenges those agencies face constantly increase. OD Security North America says it was awarded a contract by the Texas Department of Criminal Justice to provide SOTER RS Full Body Security Scanning Systems into TDCJ State Prison Facilities. The system can interface directly with a Jail Management System, which the company presents as a way to reduce processing time.

THEIA, the automatic threat recognition software, uses Artificial Intelligence to highlight and identify anomalies in scan images and flag them to the Operator. THEIA was trained on large collections of negative body scan images so that it can recognize anything that should not be part of a full body scan.

quote.text: The challenges facing Law Enforcement, Corrections and Community Justice Agencies constantly increase. The nature and type of contraband continues to change.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "© AT&T Intellectual Property. All rights reserved. FirstNet and the FirstNet logo are registered trademarks and service marks of the First Responder Network Authority." Fetched https://www.firstnet.com. The entity question in the CAUTION resolves cleanly: the footer copyright is AT&T's ('© AT&T Intellectual Property'), while the FirstNet marks are acknowledged as belonging to the First Responder Network Authority — i.e. this domain is the AT&T-operated commercial service, which is exactly the board entity 'FirstNet, Built with AT&T'. I confirmed the split by also fetching the federal side: firstnetauthority.gov states 'The First Responder Network Authority is an independent agency within the U.S. Department of Commerce's National Telecommunications and Information Administration' and sends users elsewhere for service with 'Access my FirstNet account (FirstNet.com).' So .gov is the agency, .com is the AT&T service. On rule 3: firstnet.com is NOT the parent's corporate domain (that is att.com) — it is the product's own dedicated domain with its own branding, plans and support, so it is acceptable. FLAG for the board operator, though: FirstNet does not recruit as a separate employer. Sales roles on this product are posted as AT&T requisitions, so a scraper pointed at firstnet.com will like

paragraphs: DroneShield sells counter-drone technology, which it calls counter-UAS, to military, government, law enforcement and critical infrastructure operators around the world. The company describes a portfolio that spans RF intelligence, AI, sensor fusion and software. The stated aim is to help customers detect, understand and defeat increasingly complex drone threats. Engineering, manufacturing and support are spread across Australia, the United States and Europe.

One current product, RfRecon, runs on an AI engine called RfAI-3 and detects, classifies and geolocates AIS/ADS-B signals, unencrypted Remote ID beacons and other RF activity across the spectrum. It interoperates with ATAK-CIV, SAPIENT and third-party command-and-control platforms. Deploying several units across distributed sites yields what the company calls network-scale intelligence.
DroneShield was founded in 2014 with a single focus on countering the threat posed by drones. The company began in Virginia in the United States. DroneShield Limited is publicly listed on the ASX.

paragraphs: TCP Software sells scheduling, time, and attendance solutions to organizations of any size or sector. The range covers automated time and attendance, employee scheduling, time clock hardware, and integrations for ERP, HCM, and payroll systems. TimeClock Plus covers time tracking, leave and accrual management, and K-12 resource management.

Humanity Schedule builds and adjusts shifts automatically, using AI to forecast demand and match qualified staff to shifts. It connects to payroll, ERP, or HCM software from providers including ADP, Oracle, Workday, and BambooHR, or through an open API. Humanity Time is offered to smaller teams for tracking time, attendance, and labor costs.

Aladtec is the public safety product, sold for 24/7 rotational scheduling to fire, EMS, law enforcement, and corrections agencies. Its schedules carry work, union, and fatigue rules so that an agency can answer an audit.

quote.text: 24/7 automated staff scheduling built for the unique rotation patterns and union policies of public safety and government agencies.

provenance.quote: No matter your organization’s size or sector, TCP has the scheduling, time, and attendance solutions you need to control labor costs, reduce compliance risk, and run your operations more effectively at any scale.
Secure, scalable integrations for your ERP, HCM, and payroll systems to help your teams get more done.
K-12 time tracking and resource management
Use Humanity Schedule’s AI capabilities to forecast demand, auto-build compliant schedules, and match available, qualified staff to shifts.
Already use ADP, Oracle, Workday, BambooHR, or another provider? Humanity Schedule plugs right into the current payroll, ERP, or HCM software you already use. Or build your own with our open API.
For smaller teams looking for scalable automation, Humanity Time helps you track time, attendance, and labor costs essential to small business workflows.
Aladtec scheduling software helps fire, EMS, law enforcement, and corrections agencies ensure shift coverage, comply with union and labor rules, and retain employees.
Aladtec builds your work, union, and fatigue rules right into every schedule, so you can walk into any audit knowing you’re already covered.

paragraphs: AirSight sells a drone detection software platform called AirGuard that gives security teams the real-time location of drones and of their pilots. Detection layers offered are Remote ID, RF and DF, radar and camera. The company does not build the sensors itself and describes itself as a software and systems integration business that sources hardware from partners.

The site describes buyers including airports, stadiums, prisons, universities, army bases and Fortune 500 companies. Case files name the University of Kentucky, Camping World Stadium and the Chula Vista Police Department, whose own drone flights get third-party tracking. A Complete Tier adds radar for drones that do not transmit signals, plus staff who visually confirm alerts around the clock.

AirSight was established in 2003 as 911Security. Robert Tabbara, its President and Owner, started the business after the attacks of 9/11 2001. The move into drone detection software came in July 2019. Headquarters is in Dallas, TX, with offices in Chicago, IL and Pune, India, and the company is a registered Small Business Enterprise and Public Works Contractor.

before.name: Alertus Technologies
before.description: Emergency mass notification hardware and software for schools and agencies - exhibited at EDUCAUSE 2026

paragraphs: Alertus Technologies sells emergency notification hardware and software that organizations install to warn everyone on a site at once. The company positions itself as a single source for mass emergency notification systems and critical communication needs. Its stated goal is to help colleges and universities, K-12 schools, corporations and government organizations solve unified mass notification problems.

The approach is network based, using an organization's existing IP network to turn VoIP phones into alerting devices. Hardware fills the gaps, including a wall-mounted alerting device meant for places with no existing notification endpoints. Outdoor coverage is handled by high power speaker arrays.

The company traces its origin to 2001, when an F3 tornado ripped through the University of Maryland campus. Alertus was founded the following year. It reports serving more than 2,500 organizations across more than 40 countries. Those customers are described as spanning higher education, K-12, industrial, corporate, healthcare, government and military sectors.

before.name: Regroup Mass Notification
before.description: Emergency and routine mass notification for cities, counties and schools - exhibited at APCO 2026

paragraphs: Regroup sells a mass notification platform that organizations use for emergency alerts and for everyday operational messages in one place. Government buyers use it to reach residents quickly and to improve communication among their own staff.

Alerts go out by text message, email, voice call, and social media. Messages can be aimed at a specific area through geofencing. Recipients can reply, so senders learn who is safe and who needs help. The platform also connects to federal and regional public warning systems. For larger incidents, a dashboard gives one interface for monitoring every part of an event as it unfolds.

Regroup dates its service to 2006. The company says onboarding, unlimited training, and around the clock support come at no extra cost. Comments published on the site come from county emergency management offices, among other customers. Schools and campuses are another audience, with alerts for lockdowns and similar emergencies.

paragraphs: Perimeter sells a public safety platform that pairs evacuation planning with situational awareness mapping, delivered through Perimeter Plan and Perimeter Map. Perimeter Plan is used before an incident to set safe points, evacuation routes, and critical infrastructure points. During an incident, hazards, road closures, and evacuation orders are published to a map that updates for every agency and the public.

The platform is aimed at emergency managers, public information officers, law enforcement agencies, and fire departments. The public facing map is shareable to anyone needing emergency information, with no download or sign up required. Agencies can grant access to neighboring jurisdictions and mutual aid partners.

Data created in Perimeter is stored for after action analysis. Saved detail is meant to be ready to share when records are requested by stakeholders. Perimeter exports KML and GeoJSON and integrates Esri data with existing tools.

quote.text: Perimeter provides everything needed to create, manage, and communicate zones, points, and routes for emergencies and planned events.

provenance.quote: Validate your zones with Perimeter Plan, then deploy Perimeter Map to unite agencies and the public in a true Common Operating Picture.
Set your safe points, evacuation routes, and critical infrastructure points before the call ever comes in.
Publish hazards, road closures, and evacuation orders instantly. When you update the map, it updates for every agency and the public.
Perimeter empowers emergency managers, public information officers, law enforcement agencies and fire departments to plan and respond to events in real-time.
Perimeter Map is fast, intuitive, and shareable to anyone in need of emergency information, no download or sign up required.
Grant access to neighboring jurisdictions and mutual aid partners in seconds, not hours.
Leverage Perimeter's stored data to support comprehensive after action analysis.
Ensure you have every detail saved and ready to share when records are requested by your stakeholders.
We export KML, GeoJSON, and bi-directionally integrate Esri data instantly so you can plug Perimeter into your existing tools with ease.

paragraphs: Everbridge sells a platform for managing physical and digital threats from end to end. Some of it protects traveling and remote employees. Other parts are built to inform and protect citizens at scale.

The method is to identify threats, work out who and what is affected, coordinate the response, communicate, and learn from every incident. Detection draws on risk intelligence, geospatial analysis, operational data and verified external and internal sources. Messages go out across multiple channels, with more than one delivery method per contact. A separate product centralizes business continuity planning, risk assessment, dependency mapping and testing. The main platform is available in three packages aimed at different kinds of organization.

The company states it has more than 6,500 global customers. Mass notifications are put at 6 billion a year. A customer story describes Fairfax County delivering multilingual safety alerts to over a million people. It cites a Forrester study putting average return on investment for the platform at 358 percent.

paragraphs: Esri builds ArcGIS, its geographic information system software for mapping and spatial analysis. The company describes itself as the global market leader in GIS software, location intelligence, and mapping. Its stated audience is business, government, and society.

ArcGIS is presented as enterprise technology that integrates and connects data through the context of geography. The premise is that hidden patterns, trends, and relationships emerge once data is visualized and analyzed on a map. Beyond maps and analysis, the company says its technology speeds data sharing and collaboration. For agencies that want to keep everything in house, there is a self-hosted edition for mapping, analytics, and data management.

Esri says it has supported customers with geographic science and geospatial analytics since 1969. Officials working in public safety, transportation, infrastructure, health and human services, and other fields use the technology to support high-level decisions. At the local level, the company says community leaders apply it to economic development, public works, and urban planning. Published stories include the US Census Bureau modernizing its entire census process with GIS.

before.name: Baron Weather
before.description: Weather data, alerting and decision tools for government agencies

paragraphs: Baron Weather sells weather data, forecasting and alerting tools to businesses, government agencies and communities. Its catalog holds hundreds of datasets, with information down to the street level. The company argues that free or incomplete sources leave organizations either over-prepared and wasteful or under-prepared and at risk.

Baron blends data from many sources into insights using analytical processes, machine learning, and AI. Many of its products carry built-in alerting and recommended actions to guide a decision. The company also builds weather radar hardware it describes as engineered for durability and sustainability. Its forecast modeling covers atmospheric, hydrological, marine, air quality, and road surface coupled models. Content is prepackaged so it can be shared quickly and understood without expertise.

The company traces its mission to 1989, when an F4 tornado devastated parts of Huntsville, Alabama. Its customer base spans government agencies, emergency managers, small startups, and Fortune 500 companies. Baron lists ISO 9001 quality management among the credentials behind its processes. ISO 14001 environmental management is listed as well.

before.name: Ladris Technologies
before.description: AI evacuation modeling and simulation for fire and emergency managers

paragraphs: Ladris sells disaster evacuation modeling software to planners, responders, and residents. The planning product, Core, simulates evacuations, wildfire, flooding, and other hazards, and carries mitigation plans and operational tactics into a live incident. Prime provides automated decision support for incident commanders, a fire-spread model, and an evacuation tactical plan. Sentinel delivers wildfire evacuation planning, notifications, and preparedness information free to the public through Ladris Ready.

The about page describes evacuation modeling as simulating how long it takes to move a population out of a hazard's path, producing a clearance time and the choke points that drive it. Agencies define evacuation zones, model the hazard, then simulate the evacuation across the road network to find clearance times and bottlenecks. Ladris states that these simulations run in seconds, so planners can test many scenarios instead of one.

Customer stories on the homepage name Pikes Peak Region, CO, Marin County, CA, Yuba County, CA, Jefferson County, CO, County of Maui, HI, and Town of Truckee, CA. The company works with local law, fire and emergency management to configure the platform for a jurisdiction, and says most agencies are live within days. Whether a county OES, a state agency, a fire district, or a sheriff's office, the about page invites jurisdictions to get in touch.

quote.text: No one should die in a disaster.

provenance.quote: Ladris puts the world's most trusted disaster evacuation model in the hands of planners, responders, and residents.
Simulate evacuations, wildfire, flooding, and other hazards. Design mitigation plans and operational tactics, and carry these plans into a live incident.
Automated decision support for incident commanders, a validated fire-spread model and a complete evacuation tactical plan, the moment you take command.
Wildfire evacuation planning, notifications, and preparedness information delivered free to the public through Ladris Ready, our public benefit company.
Evacuation modeling is the practice of simulating how long it takes to move a population out of a hazard's path.

Agencies define evacuation zones, estimate the people and vehicles in each, model the hazard that threatens them, then simulate the evacuation across the road network to find clearance times, bottlenecks, and the order in which zones should leave.
Ladris runs these simulations in seconds, so planners can test many scenarios instead of one.
Trusted by leaders across the United States.
We work with local law, fire and emergency management to configure Ladris for your jurisdiction and operational workflows. Most agencies are live within days.
Whether you're a county OES, a state agency, a fire district, or a sheriff's office, let's talk about what disaster intelligence looks like for your community.

before.name: Juvare
before.description: WebEOC emergency operations center and incident management software

paragraphs: Juvare sells critical operations software for organizations that need to anticipate disruption and protect communities and assets. Its best-known line, WebEOC Nexus, was built for real-time coordination, routine efficiency, and incident-level accountability from a cloud-based command center.

WebEOC consolidates internal and external data sources into built-in boards so teams work from current information. During an incident, teams track incident progress, assign tasks, deploy resources, and communicate across jurisdictions. paragraphs: Motorola Solutions builds and connects technologies to protect people, property and places, supporting the collaboration between public safety agencies and enterprises. Its public safety lineup includes APX portable and mobile radios and ASTRO radio systems. On the command center side it sells NG911 call routing and call handling and Computer-Aided Dispatch. The company also designs video security and access control systems.

For police users the APX NEXT smart radio comes in single-band and multi-band configurations. The APX 8500 all-band mobile radio adds interoperability, Wi-Fi connectivity and Bluetooth in the vehicle. Vehicle routers keep first responders connected to broadband so they can reach real-time intelligence on the road. Its broadband products can run on FirstNET or on commercial carrier LTE networks. Managed, support and professional services are sold alongside to keep those systems secure and current.

Customer stories on the site include the Ouachita Parish Sheriff's Office, Peel Police, Nampa PD and York Regional Police, which serves 1.2 million residents. Hutto Independent School District uses the VB400 body camera to capture evidence in its schools. The home page announces the completed acquisition of D-Fend Solutions, which the company describes as a counter-drone technology firm.

before.name: Blackboard
before.description: Learning management system plus accessibility and analytics tools for higher education, K-12, government, and corporate training - exhibited at EDUCAUSE 2026

paragraphs: Blackboard builds the teaching and learning environment that institutions put in front of their learners. At the core is a learning management system the company describes as rebuilt from the ground up around the learner, AI-native and personalized by design. Around it sit accessibility tools meant to open learning experiences to everyone.

The accessibility product automatically remediates course content, generates alternative formats and gives an institution a real-time compliance dashboard, and it runs with other vendors' systems too. An AI assistant guides students through course related questions. Lecture capture arrives with AI-generated captions, transcripts and audio descriptions built in. Skills and competency tracking is built into the core system, and separate institutional tools handle measuring and hitting goals.

Institutions in more than 70 countries are cited as users. The company says its reach spans higher education, government, business and K-12 worldwide. Blackboard was co-founded by Matthew Pittinsky and Michael Chasen with the mission of turning the internet into an environment for teaching and learning. It dates that work back to 1997. Compliance claims include SOC 2, FERPA, GDPR, ISO 27001, 27017 and 27018, FedRAMP Class C and WCAG 2.2 AA, all audited externally. It also reports 350 or more user-requested features released in the last 12 months.

before.name: AirWorks
before.description: AI converting aerial and lidar data into CAD basemaps and site plans; on SEWP V, NCPA, OMNIA contracts

paragraphs: AirWorks turns raw field data into mapping deliverables that engineering teams can work from. Its customers are teams in the telecom, power and civil sectors.

Source material can be lidar, orthomosaics, satellite imagery or drone capture. Patented models trained on thousands of miles of infrastructure data use computer vision to automate feature extraction, vectorization and data processing. A team of geospatial experts based in the United States reviews each output before it is delivered. More than a hundred deliverable layers are available, covering roads, curbs, sidewalks, pavement markings, vegetation and utilities.

For new construction the company supplies the site data engineers use to plan, design and deliver builds. On the maintenance side the same outputs are used to find vegetation risks near infrastructure and keep assets compliant. Operators also use the data to decide where to send field crews.

provenance.quote: AirWorks is your geospatial mapping data partner, using AI and human expertise to bridge the gap between raw field data and mapping deliverables for telecom and beyond.

before.name: Cambium Networks
before.description: Fixed wireless and Wi-Fi networks for cities, schools and public agencies

paragraphs: Cambium Networks sells Wi-Fi, broadband and security equipment to organizations building and running their own networks. Named markets include residential broadband and managed Wi-Fi for multifamily buildings, senior living, student housing and affordable housing.

The wireless line runs from Wi-Fi 5 access points through indoor and outdoor Wi-Fi 7 models. Service providers can also offer subscribers a managed home mesh router with cloud visibility and self-service setup. On the wired side, the switches come in indoor and ruggedized versions with Layer 2 and Layer 3 features and Power over Ethernet options for enterprise, industrial and campus sites. Devices are profiled without manual setup, and a switch configures itself as equipment is deployed, disconnected or moved. Management runs from public cloud, private cloud or a customer's own premises. Planning software models a fixed wireless link before anything is bought, weighing geography, distance, antenna height and transmit power.

Customers quoted on the homepage include a technology infrastructure manager at a county public school system. Another is an IT communications manager at a city government. The company courts school buyers directly, promoting a webinar on E-Rate funding.

Named offerings include omnichannel contact center solutions for federal and state agencies, tools to reduce SNAP error rates and case backlogs, and veteran services delivered through AI and digital transformation.

The case studies page lists state work, including a SNAP surge in Wisconsin and SNAP replacement benefits delivered in Texas after natural disasters. Another case study says the Texas Health and Human Services Commission contracted Maximus to integrate eligibility support services for TANF, SNAP, Medicaid, and CHIP. Other entries describe centralized credentialing for Medicaid provider networks in Ohio and a transition from the federal exchange to a state-based marketplace for Maine.

Federal examples on the same page include an AI-Powered Medical Records Processing System for disability benefits applications at the VA. The page also credits Maximus with supporting the modernization of HRSA’s Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network. Another entry says automation helped CMS streamline No Surprises Act case processing.

paragraphs: Skydio makes autonomous drones, along with the docks and software to run them, and sells drone programs to customers from energy networks to neighborhood precincts to battlefields. Those programs cover Drone as First Responder, automated inspection and site security. Dock for X10 positions Skydio X10 drones at a site so that missions launch remotely without anyone present. The smaller Skydio R10 puts eyes indoors before officers enter.

Skydio states that more than 1,500 public safety agencies use its drones. In a Drone as First Responder program, Skydio says its drones launch in under 20 seconds and reach incidents autonomously in under 90 seconds. DFR Command is the software from which remote operators launch and manage drones, respond to multiple calls and stream live video to patrol and command. It integrates with RapidSOS and CAD at dispatch, Axon Fusus for live operations, and automatic evidence upload into Axon Evidence. Skydio's customer stories include Brookhaven PD, which it says reached 30 second response times after deploying 8 Docks.

Skydio Site Security uses the same dock-based drones to verify alarms, patrol perimeters and deliver live visibility across a site. Video streams into Genetec or Milestone, and flights launch automatically when triggered by alarms or access control events. Skydio says its data is encrypted in transit and at rest and that it aligns to SOC 2, ISO 27001 and NIST frameworks.

paragraphs: Motorola Solutions builds and connects technologies to protect people, property and places, supporting the collaboration between public safety agencies and enterprises. Its public safety lineup includes APX portable and mobile radios and ASTRO radio systems. On the command center side it sells NG911 call routing and call handling and Computer-Aided Dispatch. The company also designs video security and access control systems.

For police users the APX NEXT smart radio comes in single-band and multi-band configurations. The APX 8500 all-band mobile radio adds interoperability, Wi-Fi connectivity and Bluetooth in the vehicle. Vehicle routers keep first responders connected to broadband so they can reach real-time intelligence on the road. Its broadband products can run on FirstNET or on commercial carrier LTE networks. Managed, support and professional services are sold alongside to keep those systems secure and current.

Customer stories on the site include the Ouachita Parish Sheriff's Office, Peel Police, Nampa PD and York Regional Police, which serves 1.2 million residents. Hutto Independent School District uses the VB400 body camera to capture evidence in its schools. The home page announces the completed acquisition of D-Fend Solutions, which the company describes as a counter-drone technology firm.

quote.text: Technologies designed to work together to help strengthen safety, everywhere

provenance.quote: We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places, enabling the collaboration between public safety agencies and enterprises that’s critical to safety and security.
APX portable & mobile radios
NG911 Call routing/Call handling
We design video security and access control solutions that lets you keep your people and property safe
Available in single-band and multi-band configurations, the APX NEXT smart radio brings usability and performance advancements to every aspect of the police radio experience.
The APX 8500 all-band mobile radio combines unlimited interoperability, secure Wi-Fi connectivity, integrated Bluetooth and purpose-built design.
Vehicle routers keep first responders connected to broadband so they can access real-time intelligence on the road.
Our broadband solutions can operate on FirstNET or commercial carrier LTE networks.
We provide managed, support and professional services to keep your solutions secure, optimized and current.
Threat monitoring and expert guidance help to protect York Regional Police’s mission-critical network, enhancing safety for the 1.2 million residents they serve.
Hutto Independent School District (ISD) relies on the VB400 body camera every day to capture evidence and foster trust in the school community.
An industry leader in counter-drone technology

Our 'Police' category is well supported by their own site, but it captures only part of the business: this is a dual public-safety/enterprise vendor, not a police-only one.

before.name: DeleteMe
before.description: Personal data removal subscription service - exhibited at NSA 2026

paragraphs: deleteme helps people find where their personal information is exposed online and works to have it removed. The company describes itself as a global privacy and digital exposure platform for individuals, families, professionals, executives, and businesses.

A free scan looks across data brokers, search engines, data breaches, the dark web, and other online sources. Signing up returns two complimentary reports showing where a person's information is currently exposed. After payment, staff process the request using both manual and automated methods, with status updates as each stage completes. Buyers can choose subscriptions for ongoing monitoring or one-time online reports for a single assessment. A companion service, CyberDeleteme, sells pay-as-you-go privacy intelligence, dark web monitoring, and cybersecurity scans.

The service was founded by Criton Tornaritis, described on the site as an accomplished attorney. The company states that it is not a data broker and does not maintain or commercially distribute databases of personal information. It also states that its reports must not be used for employment, credit, insurance, tenant screening, licensing, or other eligibility decisions. Its published case studies describe helping military officers reduce operational risk by removing exposed personal data from people-search and data broker sites.

paragraphs: Axon sells public safety agencies a connected set of hardware and software: Axon Body 4 cameras, Axon Fleet 3 cameras, TASER 10 energy weapons and drones, unified on a real-time crime center platform with an open ecosystem of integrated partners. The company describes itself as an operating system for public safety. TASER 10, its current less-lethal weapon, can deploy up to 10 individually targeted probes without reloading when de-escalation fails.

Axon Fusus puts officer location, alerts, dispatch data, ALPR overlays and video feeds on a single live map so command, field and real-time crime center teams work from the same picture. Residents and businesses can opt in through Community Connect to share their camera video, and those cameras then appear on the Fusus map. The Axon AI Era Plan bundles current and future Axon AI products for a fixed annual cost. Among them is Draft One, which generates first-draft report narratives from audio transcripts of digital evidence and details the officer narrates. Axon Assistant, a voice assistant on the Body 4 camera, translates conversations when no human interpreter is available.

Chief Gary Berg of Campbell PD is quoted saying Fusus lets him see live location, alerts and video from body cams, drones and public safety cameras in one platform. Axon says it is on a mission to cut gun-related deaths between police and the public in half by 2033 through technology, training and trust.

paragraphs: CyberNut sells phishing simulation training and email threat response to K-12 school districts, for staff and for students. It presents itself as a cheaper, education-first option next to the enterprise awareness vendors it names.

before.name: Ativion
before.description: ContentKeeper web filtering and StudentKeeper student safety monitoring software for K-12 school districts - exhibited at CoSN 2026

paragraphs: Ativion sells software that K-12 school districts use to filter what students can reach online and to watch for signs that a student is at risk. The StudentKeeper side of the product handles classroom management and digital safety together, reporting into one place.

Filtering under the ContentKeeper name runs partly on district hardware and partly in the cloud, with one console covering both. Because it filters at the network layer, it reaches district-managed endpoints, personal devices, guest access and connected equipment alike. Districts can run it in the cloud, on premises, or as a mix, and set rules down to the level of individual sites.

The company says it has been in technology since 2002, serving education and enterprise customers with remote access and security products as well. Its lineup came together through acquisitions that included Netop and ContentKeeper, and the Ativion name itself dates to a 2024 rebrand.

paragraphs: Procore sells construction project management software for projects from preconstruction to closeout. The products page lists capabilities to plan, prep, build, and operate construction projects on one platform. Those capabilities include bid management, budgets, drawings, daily logs, scheduling, and equipment tracking.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "© AT&T Intellectual Property. All rights reserved. FirstNet and the FirstNet logo are registered trademarks and service marks of the First Responder Network Authority." Fetched https://www.firstnet.com. The entity question in the CAUTION resolves cleanly: the footer copyright is AT&T's ('© AT&T Intellectual Property'), while the FirstNet marks are acknowledged as belonging to the First Responder Network Authority — i.e. this domain is the AT&T-operated commercial service, which is exactly the board entity 'FirstNet, Built with AT&T'. I confirmed the split by also fetching the federal side: firstnetauthority.gov states 'The First Responder Network Authority is an independent agency within the U.S. Department of Commerce's National Telecommunications and Information Administration' and sends users elsewhere for service with 'Access my FirstNet account (FirstNet.com).' So .gov is the agency, .com is the AT&T service. On rule 3: firstnet.com is NOT the parent's corporate domain (that is att.com) — it is the product's own dedicated domain with its own branding, plans and support, so it is acceptable. FLAG for the board operator, though: FirstNet does not recruit as a separate employer. Sales roles on this product are posted as AT&T requisitions, so a scraper pointed at firstnet.com will like

before.name: Oracle Utilities
before.description: Metering, CIS, billing and grid analytics for public power utilities

paragraphs: Oracle Utilities sells software to energy and water providers for serving customers and for managing networks and assets. Billing is presented as one place holding the data, processes and insights a utility needs.

Billing workflows use AI anomaly detection intended to cut errors on complex accounts. The outage management system is deployed for electric, gas, water or wastewater networks and coordinates restoration with field, mutual aid and asset management teams. Field crews record network updates straight into the network management system rather than relaying them verbally to control room staff. Analytics tools look for trends among customers and pick out electric vehicle owners for targeted recommendations and service. A commercial account product pulls billing history, consumption, appointment scheduling and service interruptions into a single dashboard.

The outage page states more than 60 million meters in production worldwide. The industry page counts 3.8 trillion AMI data reads managed annually. Those figures carry a footnote saying they are calculated from client deployments from 2009 through 2024. Oracle also cites recognition as a leader in the 2025 IDC MarketScape for utility meter data management.

paragraphs: Esri builds ArcGIS, its geographic information system software for mapping and spatial analysis. The company describes itself as the global market leader in GIS software, location intelligence, and mapping. Its stated audience is business, government, and society.

ArcGIS is presented as enterprise technology that integrates and connects data through the context of geography. The premise is that hidden patterns, trends, and relationships emerge once data is visualized and analyzed on a map. Beyond maps and analysis, the company says its technology speeds data sharing and collaboration. For agencies that want to keep everything in house, there is a self-hosted edition for mapping, analytics, and data management.

Esri says it has supported customers with geographic science and geospatial analytics since 1969. Officials working in public safety, transportation, infrastructure, health and human services, and other fields use the technology to support high-level decisions. At the local level, the company says community leaders apply it to economic development, public works, and urban planning. Published stories include the US Census Bureau modernizing its entire census process with GIS.

before.name: Govstack
before.description: CMS, online forms, events, and citizen portal platform for municipal and local government websites - exhibited at 3CMA 2026

paragraphs: Govstack sells website and online service software to public sector organizations, giving them tools to engage and connect with their communities. The audience is city staff along with the residents, visitors and business owners who need access to city services and information.

The content management system is built for public sector organizations that require full control of their site content. Staff publish without developers, because no coding or technical skills are required to build a site. The forms product carries municipal services online, with customizable workflows for applications and permits and data collected and analyzed in real time. A citizen portal gives residents one login to find information, pay for taxes and licenses, and get real-time updates on what is happening across the city. An events product sends reminders, takes registrations, processes payments and lets residents add events to their personal calendar.

Govstack states that its forms are built to comply with accessibility and WCAG 2.0 AA standards. Buyers can also draw on a library of forms developed and used by GHD Digital public sector clients. The company says it is an active member of several public sector focused associations across North America.

paragraphs: EnSoftek sells DrCloudEHR, an electronic health record the company says is built exclusively for behavioral health. It pairs clinical workflow management with revenue cycle automation and AI-assisted documentation in a single platform.

The record handles scheduling, documentation, treatment planning, ePrescribing, eMAR, group therapy, and telehealth. On the billing side, the company says it automates coding, claim submission, denial prevention, and cash flow. A scribe tool listens during patient encounters and drafts structured SOAP notes.

EnSoftek dates its founding to 2001 and says it has served more than 170 organizations nationwide. It lists headquarters in Oregon with regional offices in Chicago, Washington, DC, and India. More than 70 staff members work on developing, implementing, and supporting healthcare software. The company also states that it achieved Meaningful Use Stage 3 Promoting Interoperability certification. It sells to government buyers as well, describing itself as a managed services firm serving federal, state and local agencies.

before.name: Identity Automation
before.description: Identity and access management, rostering and access governance for K-12 school districts and universities - exhibited at CoSN 2026

hiring.note: board is another company's - not read

paragraphs: Identity Automation sells identity and access management software built for education. Its platform, RapidIdentity, covers single sign-on, application rostering, authentication methods, and password management. The company argues that real identity and access management goes beyond student rostering and single sign-on.

The lifecycle product automates provisioning, deprovisioning, account changes, credential monitoring, and access management for students, staff, partners, and vendors. The governance product automatically identifies orphan accounts in target systems. Login options include QR codes, pictographs, and challenge response questions. A web application firewall called ShieldID lets administrators prevent access outside parameters they set.

The company says RapidIdentity has managed identities at a country level in Norway, a state level in North Carolina, and across entire college systems. It claims availability rates of higher than 99.99% while serving millions of students and educators every day. One case study covers the Virginia Community College System, which the site says serves over 1.2 million identities across 23 colleges statewide. The site also reports that Jamf has acquired the company.

paragraphs: CITIZ3N Government Solutions builds modular platforms for government agencies that oversee Affordable Care Act marketplaces, Medicaid, health and human services programs, and health benefits for government employees. It is a subsidiary of Softheon and one of three brands in that portfolio.

There are two platforms: MARKETPLACE, a set of stand-alone modules meant to integrate into marketplace exchanges for government, and VERIFY, which handles eligibility determinations and combats fraud, waste, and abuse in Medicaid and HHS programs. Both are delivered as cloud-based software as a service. The architecture is cloud-native and uses an enterprise service bus for communication and interoperability between systems. The company says the platforms scale to more than a million transactions per day.

The buyers are local, state, and federal agencies. The company states compliance with HIPAA and regular security audits against frameworks such as NIST 800-53 and MARS-E 2.0. Its annual audits are listed as SOC 1 and 2, PCI AOC, a NACHA audit, penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, and code security scanning. Support is described as implementation assistance, training programs, and ongoing technical help.

paragraphs: Motorola Solutions builds and connects technologies to protect people, property and places, supporting the collaboration between public safety agencies and enterprises. Its public safety lineup includes APX portable and mobile radios and ASTRO radio systems. On the command center side it sells NG911 call routing and call handling and Computer-Aided Dispatch. The company also designs video security and access control systems.

For police users the APX NEXT smart radio comes in single-band and multi-band configurations. The APX 8500 all-band mobile radio adds interoperability, Wi-Fi connectivity and Bluetooth in the vehicle. Vehicle routers keep first responders connected to broadband so they can reach real-time intelligence on the road. Its broadband products can run on FirstNET or on commercial carrier LTE networks. Managed, support and professional services are sold alongside to keep those systems secure and current.

Customer stories on the site include the Ouachita Parish Sheriff's Office, Peel Police, Nampa PD and York Regional Police, which serves 1.2 million residents. Hutto Independent School District uses the VB400 body camera to capture evidence in its schools. The home page announces the completed acquisition of D-Fend Solutions, which the company describes as a counter-drone technology firm.

Vehicle routers keep first responders connected to broadband so they can access real-time intelligence on the road.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "AWS is the world's most comprehensive cloud, enabling organizations to accelerate innovation, reduce costs, and scale more efficiently" The URL is factually correct and does NOT violate the parent-domain rule: aws.amazon.com is AWS's own canonical property (its own brand, console, pricing, docs and its own careers page at https://aws.amazon.com/careers/, HTTP 200), not Amazon's corporate site at amazon.com. The govtech tie is on-domain too: https://aws.amazon.com/government-education/ (HTTP 200) is AWS's public sector page, and the homepage names 'AWS GovCloud (US-East)' and 'AWS GovCloud (US-West)'. MY JUDGMENT ON WHETHER THE BOARD SHOULD CARRY THIS AT ALL - the URL passes but the record is still risky, for a reason the URL check cannot fix: aws.amazon.com/careers/ does not host jobs, it hands off to https://www.amazon.jobs/en/business_categories/amazon-web-services. That feed is tens of thousands of global AWS engineering/PM/ops roles, of which SLED account executive roles are a tiny fraction. Any homepage- or careers-page-level scrape of this record will flood SLED JOBS with irrelevant listings - the same practical damage the parent-domain rule exists to prevent, arriving by a different route. Recommendation: keep the URL if AWS is wanted on the board, but the record must be wired to

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "PowerDMS by NEOGOV" DUPLICATE RECORD - board ids 'power-dms-by-neogov' and 'powerdms-by-neogov' are ONE COMPANY recorded twice. Same vendor, same product, same domain; the only difference is the spacing in the name ('Power DMS' vs 'PowerDMS'). These need MERGING into a single record, not two copies of the same website. URL itself verifies: fetched https://www.powerdms.com, which is live and carries 'PowerDMS by NEOGOV' branding in both header and footer, and sells 'PowerPolicy' for policy management and 'PowerStandards' for accreditation management, helping agencies 'manage, maintain, and prove agency-wide compliance' - matching the description exactly. Rule 3 satisfied: powerdms.com is the acquired brand's OWN domain, not the parent's corporate site (neogov.com is only a nav link out to 'NEOGOV - Public Sector HR Solutions'). paragraphs: PowerDMS by NEOGOV sells a public safety management system that brings policy, training, scheduling and compliance workflows onto one platform. Separate modules cover policy management, accreditation management, internal affairs, early intervention, field training, off duty scheduling, background investigations and text messaging surveys. The solution list carries both a public safety version and a healthcare version of policy management and of accreditation management.

Buyers named on the site include sworn officers, command staff and first responders who must meet state and federal reporting mandates. Named customers include the Lake Worth Police Department, the Cleveland Police Department and the Boulder Police Department. Testimonials also come from a county sheriff's office, a county communications center and a state law enforcement division.

Pricing is an annual subscription tailored to agency size, product selection and integrations. The software is cloud-based and requires no servers or maintenance. The site states that over 5,500 agencies use PowerDMS by NEOGOV.

paragraphs: Ativion sells software that K-12 school districts use to filter what students can reach online and to watch for signs that a student is at risk. The StudentKeeper side of the product handles classroom management and digital safety together, reporting into one place.

Filtering under the ContentKeeper name runs partly on district hardware and partly in the cloud, with one console covering both. Because it filters at the network layer, it reaches district-managed endpoints, personal devices, guest access and connected equipment alike. Districts can run it in the cloud, on premises, or as a mix, and set rules down to the level of individual sites.

The company says it has been in technology since 2002, serving education and enterprise customers with remote access and security products as well. Its lineup came together through acquisitions that included Netop and ContentKeeper, and the Ativion name itself dates to a 2024 rebrand.

paragraphs: Edovo provides free rehabilitation, upskilling, and education to incarcerated people in America. The organization describes its status as a nonprofit. Its programming is accessible on every connected device in jails and prisons, at no cost to the incarcerated learner.

Material runs from basic literacy and GED preparation to college courses and high-demand vocational training. The organization operates exclusively in the corrections space. Facility staff get tools to assess learner progress, create assignments, and digitize programs. Time served can turn into high school diplomas, college credits, workforce certifications, and earned-time credits. Other work prepares returning citizens for life outside prison.

One page states that it serves over a thousand correctional facilities and nearly a million incarcerated learners nationwide. Another page puts the count at 1,500+ prisons and jails across America. The site traces the organization to founder Brian Hill and the idea that breaking the cycle of incarceration starts with access to education. Learner testimonials are published with likenesses changed by AI to protect privacy.

brands.name: NextRec (formerly PerfectMind)
brands.description:
PerfectMind is the former name of the product now sold as nextRec, and nextrec.com keeps a page for it that opens "PerfectMind Software is now nextRec". That page defines the product as "a frictionless, all-in-one recreation management software designed for government agencies and private recreation facilities", and says PerfectMind "serves parks and recreation organizations, martial arts studios, higher-education recreation centers, swim schools, homeowner associations, and facilities offering classes and camps to their community members". The government function is the registration-and-facilities back office of a parks and recreation department: online and on-site registration for "courses, private lessons, drop ins", an "intelligent conflict manager" for scheduling community events, one-time and recurring facility rentals with customizable contract templates and digital customer signatures, point of sale for memberships and passes, built-in email marketing so departments do not sync to outside software, and real-time reporting across "any object or table in your database". A Citywide POS module is offered to consolidate payments across a municipality. The brand still has live surfaces: the knowledge base and user community on nextrec.com both sit at community.perfectmind.com, and the PCI DSS certificate the site links to is filed as "PerfectMind PCI DSS Certificate".

The page gives the family history plainly. "PerfectMind was founded in 1998." "PerfectMind's software was acquired by Xplor Technologies in 2020. In 2022, PerfectMind rebranded to become nextRec." On what changed: "The PerfectMind software platform remains built and powered by the same team - aside from changing its name to nextRec the only change is that PerfectMind software is now part of a global ecosystem with powerful backing, integrations, and support." That answers the "why does this one exist" question differently from its siblings: PerfectMind is not a separate product sitting beside nextRec, it is the same product under its previous name, kept addressable because agencies bought it under that name. The same page says "Xplor Technologies is the parent company of PerfectMind" and that Xplor "serves over 140 markets globally, 75,000 customers daily, and employs over 2,000 Xplorers across the globe". One conflict is worth recording rather than resolving: nextrec.com says PerfectMind was founded in 1998, while Xplor's corporate site says "Founded in 1988, NextRec". Both are the family's own materials and they disagree; neither was treated as settled here.

brands.name: ePACT
brands.description:
ePACT Network sells emergency and health forms automation, described on its homepage as "Emergency and health forms automation that integrates seamlessly with rec management systems" and on its parks and recreation page as a way for "rec leaders to collect, manage and access health & emergency information, waivers and consent forms - all in one secure, compliant platform". The government function is narrow and specific: it is the participant-paperwork layer under a parks and recreation department's programs. The site lists what it collects - "emergency forms with contact information and instructions, medical forms, waivers, consent forms, and personal health and safety needs", plus immunization records, medication authorization forms, allergies, dietary restrictions, medical history and signed consent forms. Named capabilities are configurable eForms, online and offline access, multi-channel communications, search, filtering and reporting, API integration, and paperless check-in and check-out with a "tailorable contact pick up list" for who may collect a child. Buyers named on the site are parks and recreation departments, YMCAs, camps and JCCs, schools, and sports associations. Public-sector customers quoted by name include the City of Kettering, OH, the San Francisco Recreation & Park Department, CA, the City of Newton Parks & Recreation, MA, the Town of Cary, NC, and the Deerfield Park District, IL. On compliance the site claims SOC II Type 2, HIPAA in the US, and PIPA, PIPEDA and FOIPPA in Canada, hosted on Microsoft Azure. Families use it free, storing a "Private Personal Emergency Record (PPER)".

ePACT sits differently in the family from the other brands: it is not a system of record for registration, it is the forms layer that attaches to one. Its own site says it integrates "with your existing registration system, like ActiveNet, Daxko, RecTrac (and more!)" - RecTrac being the sibling Vermont Systems product, ActiveNet and Daxko being competitors of the family. That is the answer to why it exists alongside three registration platforms: it is sold across all of them, including rivals. Its distribution runs through associations rather than the Xplor brand - it is "Exclusive Partner of the NRPA" with member discounts, a "Preferred vendor of the YMCA of the USA", and an "Emergency-supplies partner with the Canadian Red Cross". The family tie is real but quiet: the site footer reads "2026 ePACT Network | All Rights Reserved", with no Xplor copyright, yet it carries an Xplor Recreation logo image linking to cehrecreation.com, and ePACT is not one of the four brands listed on Xplor's own Xplor Recreation page. Its origin is on its about page: ePACT was inspired by a friend, Ayumi, separated from her two daughters during the 2011 earthquake and tsunami in Japan, and unable to learn they were safe for a full day.

paragraphs: nextRec sells cloud based software for running parks and recreation departments, from program registration to facility rentals, with a self service side for residents. Buyers range from small villages to large counties and the government staff in between.

Staff set up single or recurring classes, courses, drop-ins, and programs, with conflict checking built in. The booking side covers indoor and outdoor facilities, parks, fields, campgrounds, meeting spaces, and party venues. Payments, memberships, and product sales run through the same system, online or on-site. Reports can be created, run, and exported in real time.

The same platform is marketed to K-12 schools and to higher education institutions. Associations use it so members can pay and manage their own accounts at any hour. The company says the platform complies with PCI, ISO, and SOC standards. Customers keep ownership of their data, which the site says stays in its country of origin. Support is offered 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

brands.name: NextRec (formerly PerfectMind)
brands.description:
PerfectMind is the former name of the product now sold as nextRec, and nextrec.com keeps a page for it that opens "PerfectMind Software is now nextRec". That page defines the product as "a frictionless, all-in-one recreation management software designed for government agencies and private recreation facilities", and says PerfectMind "serves parks and recreation organizations, martial arts studios, higher-education recreation centers, swim schools, homeowner associations, and facilities offering classes and camps to their community members". The government function is the registration-and-facilities back office of a parks and recreation department: online and on-site registration for "courses, private lessons, drop ins", an "intelligent conflict manager" for scheduling community events, one-time and recurring facility rentals with customizable contract templates and digital customer signatures, point of sale for memberships and passes, built-in email marketing so departments do not sync to outside software, and real-time reporting across "any object or table in your database". A Citywide POS module is offered to consolidate payments across a municipality. The brand still has live surfaces: the knowledge base and user community on nextrec.com both sit at community.perfectmind.com, and the PCI DSS certificate the site links to is filed as "PerfectMind PCI DSS Certificate".

The page gives the family history plainly. "PerfectMind was founded in 1998." "PerfectMind's software was acquired by Xplor Technologies in 2020. In 2022, PerfectMind rebranded to become nextRec." On what changed: "The PerfectMind software platform remains built and powered by the same team - aside from changing its name to nextRec the only change is that PerfectMind software is now part of a global ecosystem with powerful backing, integrations, and support." That answers the "why does this one exist" question differently from its siblings: PerfectMind is not a separate product sitting beside nextRec, it is the same product under its previous name, kept addressable because agencies bought it under that name. The same page says "Xplor Technologies is the parent company of PerfectMind" and that Xplor "serves over 140 markets globally, 75,000 customers daily, and employs over 2,000 Xplorers across the globe". One conflict is worth recording rather than resolving: nextrec.com says PerfectMind was founded in 1998, while Xplor's corporate site says "Founded in 1988, NextRec". Both are the family's own materials and they disagree; neither was treated as settled here.

brands.name: ePACT
brands.description:
ePACT Network sells emergency and health forms automation, described on its homepage as "Emergency and health forms automation that integrates seamlessly with rec management systems" and on its parks and recreation page as a way for "rec leaders to collect, manage and access health & emergency information, waivers and consent forms - all in one secure, compliant platform". The government function is narrow and specific: it is the participant-paperwork layer under a parks and recreation department's programs. The site lists what it collects - "emergency forms with contact information and instructions, medical forms, waivers, consent forms, and personal health and safety needs", plus immunization records, medication authorization forms, allergies, dietary restrictions, medical history and signed consent forms. Named capabilities are configurable eForms, online and offline access, multi-channel communications, search, filtering and reporting, API integration, and paperless check-in and check-out with a "tailorable contact pick up list" for who may collect a child. Buyers named on the site are parks and recreation departments, YMCAs, camps and JCCs, schools, and sports associations. Public-sector customers quoted by name include the City of Kettering, OH, the San Francisco Recreation & Park Department, CA, the City of Newton Parks & Recreation, MA, the Town of Cary, NC, and the Deerfield Park District, IL. On compliance the site claims SOC II Type 2, HIPAA in the US, and PIPA, PIPEDA and FOIPPA in Canada, hosted on Microsoft Azure. Families use it free, storing a "Private Personal Emergency Record (PPER)".

ePACT sits differently in the family from the other brands: it is not a system of record for registration, it is the forms layer that attaches to one. Its own site says it integrates "with your existing registration system, like ActiveNet, Daxko, RecTrac (and more!)" - RecTrac being the sibling Vermont Systems product, ActiveNet and Daxko being competitors of the family. That is the answer to why it exists alongside three registration platforms: it is sold across all of them, including rivals. Its distribution runs through associations rather than the Xplor brand - it is "Exclusive Partner of the NRPA" with member discounts, a "Preferred vendor of the YMCA of the USA", and an "Emergency-supplies partner with the Canadian Red Cross". The family tie is real but quiet: the site footer reads "2026 ePACT Network | All Rights Reserved", with no Xplor copyright, yet it carries an Xplor Recreation logo image linking to cehrecreation.com, and ePACT is not one of the four brands listed on Xplor's own Xplor Recreation page. Its origin is on its about page: ePACT was inspired by a friend, Ayumi, separated from her two daughters during the 2011 earthquake and tsunami in Japan, and unable to learn they were safe for a full day.

before.name: Agents of Discovery
before.description: Mobile augmented-reality game platform licensed to airports, parks and public agencies to engage visitors with location-triggered educational missions and wayfinding-style content.

paragraphs: Agents of Discovery turns physical spaces such as museums, airports, campuses, libraries, stadiums and entire cities into interactive learning environments by blending AI-driven content generation with place-based augmented reality gameplay. Customers become what the company calls Mission Makers, turning their own stories, spaces and content into augmented reality experiences.

Location-based challenges are placed on site and tied to the customer's own content, or played from anywhere. A site can also deploy a fully customized AI avatar as its on-site guide. Self-guided tours are offered around the clock. Exhibits can be built for aquariums, zoos and museums. Text-to-speech and multiple language options are meant to keep the platform reachable for players with diverse abilities and backgrounds.

Airports are one named setting, where the pitch is turning downtime into interactive adventures built for travelers. Junior Ranger Missions on the platform cover subjects from palaeontology and fossils to International Migratory Bird Day. The chief academic officer works with public and private organizations across the United States, Australia and Canada on visitor experience. The company describes itself as a Harvard-incubated AI and augmented reality company.

paragraphs: Amilia sells software that pulls memberships, program registration, payments, and reporting into one system. The customer it describes is the community organization that runs classes, memberships, and facilities for local families.

Registration happens through a branded online store that can stand on its own or sit inside the organization's existing website. On the facilities side, a calendar keeps bookings, activities, and rental contracts in sync so staff can see which space is in use and when. Access rules decide which memberships, activities, or passes open the door at each entry point.
The company states that over 1,500 organizations have chosen it. It advertises a 99.99% uptime guarantee for round-the-clock selling. Help is offered by live chat, phone, and email.

paragraphs: FMX sells facilities and maintenance management software that organizations use to streamline processes and get more out of their assets. For cities and counties, the pitch is maximizing asset performance, allocating spaces and funding, and streamlining resident service delivery. A school edition promises facility management software that will meet a district where it is at.

Work order management streamlines request submissions and helps staff resolve maintenance issues. Preventive maintenance handles compliance and schedules recurring tasks. Reporting tracks labor hours and costs so investments can be justified. Separate products cover vehicles, keeping a fleet on the road and tracking repairs. The products are cloud-based. A 14-day free trial is offered.

The company says it serves over 400K professionals. Beyond schools it sells into public works, covering public infrastructure, assets, public property, capital projects, and community events. It points to 400+ reviews on Capterra, Software Advice, and G2. Pricing turns on how many users an organization has, or the number of students enrolled for public K-12 schools.

paragraphs: OfferioRFP sells a secure, AI-powered platform that helps small and mid-sized businesses generate compliant and professional proposals. The platform works from documents a customer supplies, and the site tells users to upload past proposals and corporate documents so the tool follows an organization's own language. Customers use it to respond to municipal, provincial/state, federal, and agency RFPs with requirement analysis and compliance alignment. An assistant inside the product interprets requirements, drafts evaluator-ready responses, validates compliance, and surfaces supporting materials. A monitoring feature surfaces public-sector RFPs so a team spends its time on qualification rather than searching.

OfferioRFP runs on OfferioAI, which the page calls a purposefully built Business AI Engine. The site claims the platform saves on average 70% of time spent on custom proposal creations. A published set of questions says the product automates both RFP discovery and response generation using existing business documents.

paragraphs: Govstream.ai sells permitting software to cities and counties, aimed at the point where an applicant is trying to work out what their project actually requires. It is positioned as an addition to the systems a city already runs rather than a replacement for them.

A research assistant answers questions about a specific property, using zoning, overlays and GIS data so an applicant can see what applies to that parcel.
